307	    async def _handle_processing_tools_state(self, agent_data: AgentData) -> AgentState:
308	        """Handle the processing tools state: execute tool calls and prepare tool responses."""
309	        add_messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
310	        new_images_this_turn: list[Any] = []  # Local variable instead of agent_data attribute
311	        previous_messages = list(agent_data.messages)
312	
313	        tasks = []
314	        tool_call_names = []
315	        for tool_call in agent_data.tool_calls[: self.max_parallel_calls]:
316	            tasks.append(self._call_tool(tool_call, agent_data.tools_kwargs, agent_data))
317	            tool_call_names.append(tool_call.name)
318	
319	        with simple_timer("tool_calls", agent_data.metrics):
320	            responses = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
321	
322	        # Process tool responses and update multi_modal_data
323	        # Removed: agent_data.new_images_this_turn = []
324	        for tool_index, (tool_response, tool_reward, _) in enumerate(responses):
325	            tool_call = agent_data.tool_calls[tool_index]
326	            # Create message from tool response
327	            if tool_response.image or tool_response.video:
328	                # Multi-modal content with structured format
329	                if not getattr(self.processor, "image_processor", None):
330	                    raise ValueError(
331	                        "Multimedia data can only be processed by `processor`, but the processor is None. "
332	                        "This error is often caused if you are using a LLM model but your tool returns multimodal "
333	                        "data. Plase use a vlm as the base model."
334	                    )
335	                content = []
336	                if tool_response.image:
337	                    content.append({"type": "image"})
338	                if tool_response.video:
339	                    content.append({"type": "video"})
340	                if tool_response.text:
341	                    content.append({"type": "text", "text": tool_response.text})
342	                message = {"role": "tool", "content": content}
343	            else:
344	                # Text-only content
345	                message = {"role": "tool", "content": tool_response.text or ""}
346	            if tool_call.tool_call_id is not None:
347	                message["tool_call_id"] = tool_call.tool_call_id
348	
349	            add_messages.append(message)
350	
351	            # Handle image data
352	            if tool_response.image:
353	                # Add new image data
354	                if isinstance(tool_response.image, list):
355	                    # Ensure all elements in the list are valid image objects
356	                    for img in tool_response.image:
357	                        if img is not None:  # Add a check to ensure the image is not None
358	                            new_images_this_turn.append(img)  # Using local variable
359	                else:
360	                    # Ensure the image is not None
361	                    if tool_response.image is not None:
362	                        new_images_this_turn.append(tool_response.image)  # Using local variable
363	
364	            # Handle video data
365	            if tool_response.video:
366	                # Currently not supported, raise informative error
367	                logger.warning("Multimedia type 'video' is not currently supported. Only 'image' is supported.")
368	                raise NotImplementedError(
369	                    "Multimedia type 'video' is not currently supported. Only 'image' is supported."
370	                )
371	
372	            if tool_reward is not None:
373	                agent_data.tool_rewards.append(tool_reward)
374	
375	        agent_data.messages.extend(add_messages)
376	
377	        if self.enable_continuous_token and not new_images_this_turn:
378	            schemas = getattr(agent_data, "_active_tool_schemas", self.tool_schemas)
379	            merge_result, response_mask, response_logprobs = await self.ct_merge_non_assistant_msg(
380	                previous_messages,
381	                agent_data.messages,
382	                agent_data.prompt_ids,
383	                agent_data.response_mask,
384	                agent_data.response_logprobs if agent_data.response_logprobs else None,
385	                tools=schemas,
386	            )
387	            if len(response_mask) >= self.response_length:
388	                return AgentState.TERMINATED
389	            agent_data.prompt_ids = merge_result.token_ids
390	            agent_data.response_mask = response_mask
391	            if agent_data.response_logprobs:
392	                agent_data.response_logprobs = response_logprobs or []
393	            agent_data.user_turns += 1
394	            return AgentState.GENERATING
395	        elif self.tool_parser_name == "gpt-oss":
396	            logger.info("manually format tool responses for gpt-oss")
397	            tool_response_text = build_gpt_oss_tool_response_text(add_messages, tool_call_names)
398	            response_ids = await self.loop.run_in_executor(
399	                None, lambda: self.tokenizer.encode(tool_response_text, add_special_tokens=False)
400	            )
401	        elif self.tool_parser_name == "gemma4":
402	            # Gemma4's chat template drops tool responses when passed without the preceding
403	            # assistant tool_call message. Manually format the response tokens.
404	            # Format: <|tool_response>response:func_name{value:<|"|>content<|"|>}<tool_response|>
405	            parts = []
406	            for msg, name in zip(add_messages, tool_call_names, strict=True):
407	                content = msg.get("content", "")
408	                if isinstance(content, list):
409	                    content = "".join([item.get("text", "") for item in content if item.get("type") == "text"])
410	                parts.append(f'<|tool_response>response:{name}{{value:<|"|>{content}<|"|>}}<tool_response|>')
411	            tool_response_text = "".join(parts)
412	            response_ids = await self.loop.run_in_executor(
413	                None, lambda: self.tokenizer.encode(tool_response_text, add_special_tokens=False)
414	            )
415	        else:
416	            # Note that we have to pass None to the images and videos if there are no new images / videos
417	            # to stay compatible with downstream image processing logic!
418	            images = new_images_this_turn if new_images_this_turn else None
419	            videos = None
420	            response_ids = await self.apply_chat_template(
421	                add_messages,
422	                images=images,
423	                videos=videos,
424	                remove_system_prompt=True,
425	            )
426	            # The model stopped at the assistant close token and never emitted the template's
427	            # trailing turn separator (e.g. "\n" for Qwen); rendering this tool turn in isolation
428	            # also omits it. Restore it so the incremental sequence matches apply_chat_template of
429	            # the full conversation (see verl issue #6501 comment). ``turn_separator`` is [] for
430	            # templates without one, so this is a no-op there.
431	            response_ids = self.turn_separator + response_ids
432	
433	        if len(agent_data.response_mask) + len(response_ids) >= self.response_length:
434	            return AgentState.TERMINATED
435	        # Update prompt_ids and response_mask
436	
437	        if new_images_this_turn:
438	            if agent_data.image_data is None:
439	                agent_data.image_data = []
440	            elif not isinstance(agent_data.image_data, list):
441	                agent_data.image_data = [agent_data.image_data]
442	            for img in new_images_this_turn:
443	                agent_data.image_data.append(img)
444	
445	        agent_data.prompt_ids += response_ids
446	        agent_data.response_mask += [0] * len(response_ids)
447	        if agent_data.response_logprobs:
448	            agent_data.response_logprobs += [0.0] * len(response_ids)
449	        agent_data.user_turns += 1
450	        return AgentState.GENERATING

452	    def _build_assistant_message(self, content: str, agent_data: AgentData) -> dict[str, Any]:
453	        message: dict[str, Any] = {"role": "assistant", "content": content or ""}
454	        if not agent_data.tool_calls:
455	            return message
456	
457	        tool_calls = []
458	        for index, tool_call in enumerate(agent_data.tool_calls[: self.max_parallel_calls]):
459	            function_call, has_decode_error = OpenAIFunctionCallSchema.from_openai_function_parsed_schema(
460	                OpenAIFunctionParsedSchema(name=tool_call.name, arguments=tool_call.arguments)
461	            )
462	            if has_decode_error:
463	                raise ValueError(
464	                    f"Invalid tool call arguments for '{tool_call.name}': expected a JSON object string, "
465	                    f"got {tool_call.arguments!r}"
466	                )
467	            tool_call_message = {
468	                "type": "function",
469	                "function": function_call.model_dump(),
470	            }
471	            if tool_call.tool_call_id is not None:
472	                tool_call_message["id"] = tool_call.tool_call_id
473	            tool_calls.append(tool_call_message)
474	        message["tool_calls"] = tool_calls
475	        return message

477	    async def _call_tool(
478	        self, tool_call: FunctionCall, tools_kwargs: dict[str, Any], agent_data: AgentData
479	    ) -> tuple[ToolResponse, float, dict]:
480	        """Call tool and return tool response.
481	
482	        Dispatches between two contracts:
483	        - ``FunctionTool``: stateless function-based tool. Invoked directly with
484	          parsed arguments; no lifecycle.
485	        - ``BaseTool`` subclass: stateful tool with full lifecycle.
486	        """
487	        active_tools = getattr(agent_data, "_active_tools", self.tools)
488	
489	        # Validate tool name
490	        tool_name = tool_call.name
491	        if tool_name not in active_tools:
492	            available = list(active_tools.keys())
493	            msg = f"Unknown function '{tool_name}'. Available tools: {available}"
494	            logger.warning(msg)
495	            return ToolResponse(text=msg), 0.0, {}
496	
497	        # Validate tool arguments
498	        try:
499	            tool_args = json.loads(tool_call.arguments)
500	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError) as e:
501	            msg = f"Invalid JSON in arguments for '{tool_name}': {e}"
502	            logger.warning(msg)
503	            return ToolResponse(text=msg), 0.0, {}
504	
505	        # Execute tool
506	        tool, instance_id = None, None
507	        try:
508	            tool = active_tools[tool_name]
509	
510	            if isinstance(tool, FunctionTool):
511	                # Function-based tools have no lifecycle; call directly.
512	                # Note: tools_kwargs (create_kwargs / release_kwargs) is intentionally
513	                # ignored here. Function tools are stateless and per-trajectory state
514	                # injection is not supported by design; use a BaseTool subclass instead.
515	                raw = await tool.call(tool_args)
516	                tool_execution_response, tool_reward, res = normalize_function_tool_return(raw)
517	            else:
518	                # BaseTool subclass
519	                kwargs = tools_kwargs.get(tool_name, {})
520	                instance_id, _ = await tool.create(create_kwargs=kwargs.get("create_kwargs", {}))
521	                tool_execution_response, tool_reward, res = await tool.execute(
522	                    instance_id, tool_args, agent_data=agent_data
523	                )
524	        except Exception as e:
525	            logger.warning(f"Error executing tool '{tool_name}': {e}")
526	            return ToolResponse(text=f"Error executing tool '{tool_name}': {e}"), 0.0, {}
527	        finally:
528	            # Only BaseTool instances need release (function tools never set instance_id).
529	            if tool and instance_id and not isinstance(tool, FunctionTool):
530	                await tool.release(instance_id)
531	
532	        tool_response_text = tool_execution_response.text
533	        if tool_response_text and len(tool_response_text) > self.max_tool_response_length:
534	            if self.tool_response_truncate_side == "left":
535	                tool_response_text = "(truncated)..." + tool_response_text[-self.max_tool_response_length :]
536	            elif self.tool_response_truncate_side == "right":
537	                tool_response_text = tool_response_text[: self.max_tool_response_length] + "...(truncated)"
538	            else:
539	                length = self.max_tool_response_length // 2
540	                tool_response_text = tool_response_text[:length] + "...(truncated)..." + tool_response_text[-length:]
541	
542	        # Create ToolResponse from tool execution result
543	        tool_response_kwargs = {"text": tool_response_text}
544	
545	        # Add multimedia data if present
546	        for attr_name in ["image", "video"]:
547	            if hasattr(tool_execution_response, attr_name):
548	                attr_value = getattr(tool_execution_response, attr_name)
549	                if attr_value is not None:
550	                    tool_response_kwargs[attr_name] = attr_value
551	
552	        return ToolResponse(**tool_response_kwargs), tool_reward, res

448	    async def run_server(self, args: argparse.Namespace):
449	        engine_args = AsyncEngineArgs.from_cli_args(args)
450	        usage_context = UsageContext.OPENAI_API_SERVER
451	        vllm_config = engine_args.create_engine_config(usage_context=usage_context)
452	        vllm_config.parallel_config.data_parallel_master_port = self._dp_master_port
453	
454	        fn_args = set(dict(inspect.signature(AsyncLLM.from_vllm_config).parameters).keys())
455	        kwargs = {}
456	        if "enable_log_requests" in fn_args:
457	            kwargs["enable_log_requests"] = engine_args.enable_log_requests
458	        if "disable_log_stats" in fn_args:
459	            kwargs["disable_log_stats"] = engine_args.disable_log_stats
460	
461	        engine_client = AsyncLLM.from_vllm_config(vllm_config=vllm_config, usage_context=usage_context, **kwargs)
462	
463	        # Don't keep the dummy data in memory
464	        await engine_client.reset_mm_cache()
465	        await engine_client.collective_rpc(
466	            method="monkey_patch_model", kwargs={"vocab_size": len(self.model_config.tokenizer)}
467	        )
468	
469	        build_app_sig = inspect.signature(build_app)
470	        supported_tasks: tuple[Any, ...] = ()
471	        build_app_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
472	        if "supported_tasks" in build_app_sig.parameters:
473	            supported_tasks = await engine_client.get_supported_tasks()
474	            build_app_kwargs["supported_tasks"] = supported_tasks
475	        # vLLM >= 0.20.0 requires `model_config` to register pooling API routes
476	        # (e.g. ``/classify``, ``/embed``); see
477	        # ``register_pooling_api_routers`` in vllm/entrypoints/pooling/factories.py
478	        # which short-circuits when ``model_config`` is ``None``.
479	        if "model_config" in build_app_sig.parameters:
480	            build_app_kwargs["model_config"] = engine_client.model_config
481	        app = build_app(args, **build_app_kwargs)
482	
483	        init_app_sig = inspect.signature(init_app_state)
484	        if "vllm_config" in init_app_sig.parameters:
485	            await init_app_state(engine_client, vllm_config, app.state, args)
486	        elif "supported_tasks" in init_app_sig.parameters:
487	            await init_app_state(engine_client, app.state, args, supported_tasks)
488	        else:
489	            await init_app_state(engine_client, app.state, args)
490	        if self.replica_rank == 0 and self.node_rank == 0:
491	            logger.info(f"Initializing a V1 LLM engine with config: {vllm_config}")
492	
493	        self.engine = engine_client
494	        self._server_port, self._server_task = await run_uvicorn(app, args, self._server_address)

496	    async def run_headless(self, args: argparse.Namespace):
497	        """Run headless server in a separate thread."""
498	        args.api_server_count = 0
499	
500	        def run_headless_wrapper():
501	            with SuppressSignalInThread():
502	                run_headless(args)
503	
504	        def on_run_headless_done(future: asyncio.Future):
505	            try:
506	                exc = future.exception()
507	                if exc:
508	                    logger.exception(f"run_headless failed with exception: {exc}")
509	                else:
510	                    logger.warning("run_headless completed successfully, but it's not expected.")
511	            except Exception as e:
512	                logger.exception(f"get result from run_headless failed: {e}")
513	            finally:
514	                os._exit(1)

519	    async def generate(
520	        self,
521	        prompt_ids: list[int],
522	        sampling_params: dict[str, Any],
523	        request_id: str,
524	        image_data: Optional[list[Any]] = None,
525	        video_data: Optional[list[Any]] = None,
526	        audio_data: Optional[list[Any]] = None,
527	        mm_processor_kwargs: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
528	        priority: int = 0,
529	        kv_transfer_params: Optional[dict] = None,
530	    ) -> TokenOutput:
531	        """Generate sequence with token-in-token-out.
532	
533	        Args:
534	            kv_transfer_params: vLLM KV-transfer payload for PD requests.
535	        """
536	        if self._disaggregation_role == "prefill" and self._pd_decode_peers and kv_transfer_params is None:
537	            return await self._pd_dispatch(
538	                prompt_ids,
539	                sampling_params,
540	                request_id,
541	                image_data=image_data,
542	                video_data=video_data,
543	                audio_data=audio_data,
544	                mm_processor_kwargs=mm_processor_kwargs,
545	                priority=priority,
546	            )
547	
548	        prompt_ids = normalize_token_ids(prompt_ids)
549	
550	        # Calculate the maximum possible new tokens based on available context space
551	        # This serves as a safety upper bound. vLLM v0.20+ rejects `max_tokens < 1`
552	        # (see vllm.sampling_params.SamplingParams._verify_args), so we require at
553	        # least one token of headroom to be able to generate at all.
554	        max_possible_tokens = self.config.max_model_len - len(prompt_ids)
555	        if max_possible_tokens < 1:
556	            raise ValueError(
557	                f"Prompt length ({len(prompt_ids)}) leaves no room to generate within the "
558	                f"model's maximum context length ({self.config.max_model_len}); need at least "
559	                f"1 token of headroom."
560	            )
561	
562	        # Determine max_tokens from sampling_params or use configured response_length as default
563	        if "max_tokens" in sampling_params:
564	            max_tokens = sampling_params.pop("max_tokens")
565	        elif "max_new_tokens" in sampling_params:
566	            # support sglang-style 'max_new_tokens' param
567	            max_tokens = sampling_params.pop("max_new_tokens")
568	        else:
569	            # Default to a calculation that considers configured lengths
570	            # Cap max_tokens by response_length to ensure tensor alignment,
571	            # and by remaining budget to prevent OOM in multi-turn rollouts.
572	            max_tokens = min(
573	                self.config.response_length, self.config.prompt_length + self.config.response_length - len(prompt_ids)
574	            )
575	
576	        # Clamp max_tokens to the valid range [1, max_possible_tokens]. The lower bound
577	        # is 1 because vLLM v0.20+ raises VLLMValidationError when max_tokens < 1.
578	        max_tokens = max(1, min(max_tokens, max_possible_tokens))
579	
580	        assert 1 <= max_tokens <= max_possible_tokens, (
581	            f"max_tokens {max_tokens} not in valid range [1, {max_possible_tokens}]"
582	        )
583	        sampling_params["logprobs"] = 0 if sampling_params.pop("logprobs", False) else None
584	        sampling_params.setdefault("repetition_penalty", self.config.get("repetition_penalty", 1.0))
585	        sampling_params.setdefault("ignore_eos", self.config.get("ignore_eos", False))
586	        # Inject per-request seed for deterministic sampling when full_determinism is enabled.
587	        if self.config.full_determinism:
588	            sampling_params.setdefault("seed", self.replica_rank + self.config.seed)
589	
590	        if kv_transfer_params is not None:
591	            extra_args = dict(sampling_params.pop("extra_args", None) or {})
592	            extra_args["kv_transfer_params"] = kv_transfer_params
593	            sampling_params["extra_args"] = extra_args
594	
595	        sampling_params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=max_tokens, **sampling_params)
596	        prompt_ids = qwen2_5_vl_dedup_image_tokens(prompt_ids, self.model_config.processor)
597	        multi_modal_data = {}
598	        if image_data is not None:
599	            multi_modal_data["image"] = image_data
600	        if video_data is not None:
601	            multi_modal_data["video"] = video_data
602	        if audio_data is not None:
603	            multi_modal_data["audio"] = audio_data
604	
605	        prompt_kwargs = {"prompt_token_ids": prompt_ids, "multi_modal_data": multi_modal_data}
606	        if mm_processor_kwargs:
607	            prompt_kwargs["mm_processor_kwargs"] = mm_processor_kwargs
608	        try:
609	            prompt = TokensPrompt(**prompt_kwargs)
610	        except TypeError:
611	            prompt = prompt_kwargs
612	
613	        # Add lora request
614	        lora_request = None
615	        if self.lora_as_adapter:
616	            # Make sure we also check that the lora is already loaded in the engine
617	            lora_loaded = VLLM_LORA_INT_ID in await self.engine.list_loras()
618	            if lora_loaded:
619	                lora_request = LoRARequest(
620	                    lora_name=VLLM_LORA_NAME, lora_int_id=VLLM_LORA_INT_ID, lora_path=VLLM_LORA_PATH
621	                )
622	
623	        generator = self.engine.generate(
624	            prompt=prompt,
625	            sampling_params=sampling_params,
626	            request_id=request_id,
627	            lora_request=lora_request,
628	            priority=priority,
629	        )
630	
631	        # Get final response
632	        final_res: Optional[RequestOutput] = None
633	        async for output in generator:
634	            final_res = output
635	        assert final_res is not None
636	
637	        extra_fields = {"global_steps": self.global_steps}
638	        # Handle abort case: when the request is aborted by pause_generation(abort),
639	        # outputs may be empty. Return empty results with stop_reason="aborted"
640	        # instead of crashing with "IndexError: list index out of range".
641	        if not final_res.outputs:
642	            return TokenOutput(
643	                token_ids=[],
644	                log_probs=None,
645	                routed_experts=None,
646	                stop_reason="aborted",
647	                extra_fields=extra_fields,
648	            )
649	
650	        extract_prompt_logprobs(
651	            output=final_res,
652	            num_prompt_logprobs=sampling_params.prompt_logprobs,
653	            result_dict=extra_fields,
654	        )
655	        token_ids = final_res.outputs[0].token_ids
656	        log_probs = None
657	        if sampling_params.logprobs is not None:
658	            log_probs = [logprobs[token_ids[i]].logprob for i, logprobs in enumerate(final_res.outputs[0].logprobs)]
659	
660	        routed_experts = None
661	        if self.config.enable_rollout_routing_replay:
662	            routed_experts = final_res.outputs[0].routed_experts
663	
664	        # Determine stop reason from finish_reason
665	        finish_reason = final_res.outputs[0].finish_reason
666	        if finish_reason == "abort":
667	            stop_reason = "aborted"
668	        elif finish_reason in ("stop", "length"):
669	            stop_reason = "completed"
670	        else:
671	            stop_reason = finish_reason  # for more stop reason in the future
672	
673	        num_preempted = None
674	
675	        if hasattr(final_res.outputs[0], "num_preempted"):
676	            num_preempted = final_res.outputs[0].num_preempted
677	
678	        response_kv_transfer_params = getattr(final_res, "kv_transfer_params", None)
679	        if response_kv_transfer_params is not None:
680	            extra_fields["kv_transfer_params"] = response_kv_transfer_params
681	
682	        # Re-key backend spec-decoding stats to the rollout-common names.
683	        if self.config.mtp is not None and self.config.mtp.enable and self.config.mtp.enable_rollout:
684	            spec_decode_stats = getattr(final_res.metrics, "request_spec_decode_stats", None)
685	            if spec_decode_stats is None:
686	                if not self._warned_missing_spec_decode_stats:
687	                    logger.warning(
688	                        "vLLM MTP rollout metrics do not include request_spec_decode_stats; "
689	                        "speculative decoding acceptance metrics will be skipped."
690	                    )
691	                    self._warned_missing_spec_decode_stats = True
692	            else:
693	                extra_fields["spec_num_draft_tokens"] = spec_decode_stats.num_draft_tokens
694	                extra_fields["spec_num_accepted_tokens"] = spec_decode_stats.num_accepted_tokens
695	                extra_fields["spec_num_verify_steps"] = spec_decode_stats.num_verify_steps
696	        return TokenOutput(
697	            token_ids=token_ids,
698	            log_probs=log_probs,
699	            routed_experts=routed_experts,
700	            stop_reason=stop_reason,
701	            num_preempted=num_preempted,
702	            extra_fields=extra_fields,
703	        )

711	    async def _pd_dispatch(

861	    async def abort_all_requests(self, reset_prefix_cache: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:
862	        """Abort all ongoing generation requests.
863	
864	        On vLLM >= 0.12.0, uses AsyncLLM.pause_generation() to abort in-flight
865	        requests, drain, and clear caches. The engine remains paused after this
866	        call — use resume_generation() to accept new requests (e.g. before
867	        validation).
868	
869	        On vLLM < 0.12.0, manually aborts each request and resets prefix cache.
870	
871	        Returns:
872	            dict[str, Any]: Dictionary containing:
873	                - aborted_count: Number of requests aborted
874	                - request_ids: List of aborted request IDs
875	        """
876	        try:
877	            if _VLLM_VERSION >= version.parse("0.12.0"):
878	                # Snapshot request IDs before pausing for reporting
879	                request_ids = list(self.engine.output_processor.request_states.keys())
880	
881	                # pause_generation with wait_for_inflight_requests=False will:
882	                # 1. Set engine to paused state (blocks new generate calls)
883	                # 2. Abort all in-flight requests
884	                # 3. Wait for requests to drain
885	                # 4. Clear prefix and mm caches if clear_cache=True.
886	                #    EngineCore._reset_caches defaults reset_connector=True
887	                #    on this path, so any attached external KV store (e.g.
888	                #    MooncakeStoreConnector) is invalidated along with the
889	                #    local prefix cache — RL-correct hard-reset at every
890	                #    weight update boundary, no extra kwargs needed.
891	                await self.engine.pause_generation(
892	                    wait_for_inflight_requests=False,
893	                    clear_cache=reset_prefix_cache,
894	                )
895	            else:
896	                # Take an atomic snapshot to avoid race conditions with the vLLM engine thread
897	                request_states_snapshot = list(self.engine.output_processor.request_states.items())
898	                request_ids = [req_id for req_id, _ in request_states_snapshot]
899	
900	                if not request_ids:
901	                    return {"aborted_count": 0, "request_ids": []}
902	
903	                # For each request, create an abort output and put it to its queue
904	                # This allows the generator to receive the aborted result
905	                from vllm.v1.engine import FinishReason
906	
907	                for _, req_state in request_states_snapshot:
908	                    request_output = req_state.make_request_output(
909	                        [], pooling_output=None, finish_reason=FinishReason.ABORT, stop_reason=None
910	                    )
911	                    req_state.queue.put(request_output)
912	
913	                # Abort requests in the output processor and engine core
914	                self.engine.output_processor.abort_requests(request_ids)
915	                await self.engine.engine_core.abort_requests_async(request_ids)
916	
917	                # Try to reset prefix cache to ensure clean state
918	                if reset_prefix_cache:
919	                    await self.clear_kv_cache()
920	                    logger.info("Prefix cache reset after abort")
921	
922	            logger.info(f"Aborted {len(request_ids)} requests: {request_ids}")
923	            return {"aborted_count": len(request_ids), "request_ids": request_ids}
924	
925	        except Exception as e:
926	            logger.error(f"Error aborting requests: {e}")
927	            return {"aborted_count": 0, "request_ids": [], "error": str(e)}
928	
929	    async def resume_generation(self):
930	        """Resume generation after abort_all_requests (pause_generation).
931	
932	        Only effective on vLLM >= 0.12.0 where pause_generation is used.
933	        No-op on older versions.
934	        """
935	        if self.node_rank != 0:
936	            return

938	            await self.engine.resume_generation()

940	    async def abort_request(self, request_id: str, reset_prefix_cache: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:
941	        """Abort a specific generation request.
942	
943	        Args:
944	            request_id: The ID of the request to abort.
945	
946	        Returns:
947	            dict[str, Any]: Dictionary containing abort result.
948	        """
949	        try:
950	            request_states = self.engine.output_processor.request_states
951	            req_state = request_states.get(request_id)
952	
953	            if req_state is None:
954	                return {"aborted": False, "error": f"Request {request_id} not found"}
955	
956	            # Create abort output and put it to the queue
957	            from vllm.v1.engine import FinishReason
958	
959	            request_output = req_state.make_request_output(
960	                [], pooling_output=None, finish_reason=FinishReason.ABORT, stop_reason=None
961	            )
962	            req_state.queue.put(request_output)
963	
964	            # Abort in output processor and engine core
965	            self.engine.output_processor.abort_requests([request_id])
966	            await self.engine.engine_core.abort_requests_async([request_id])
967	
968	            # Try to reset prefix cache to ensure clean state
969	            if reset_prefix_cache:
970	                await self.clear_kv_cache()
971	                logger.info(f"Prefix cache reset after abort request {request_id}")
972	
973	            logger.info(f"Aborted request: {request_id}")
974	            return {"aborted": True, "request_id": request_id}
975	
976	        except Exception as e:
977	            logger.error(f"Error aborting request {request_id}: {e}")
978	            return {"aborted": False, "request_id": request_id, "error": str(e)}

1575	    # exp [(1/|y_i|) * Σ_t log(π_θ(y_i,t|x,y_i,<t)/π_θold(y_i,t|x,y_i,<t))]
1576	    seq_lengths = torch.sum(response_mask, dim=-1).clamp(min=1)
1577	    negative_approx_kl_seq = torch.sum(negative_approx_kl * response_mask, dim=-1) / seq_lengths
1578	
1579	    # Combined ratio at token level:
1580	    # s_i,t(θ) = sg[s_i(θ)] · π_θ(y_i,t|x, y_i,<t) / sg[π_θ(y_i,t|x, y_i,<t)]
1581	    # In log space: log(s_i,t(θ)) = sg[log(s_i(θ))] + log_prob - sg[log_prob]
1582	    log_seq_importance_ratio = log_prob - log_prob.detach() + negative_approx_kl_seq.detach().unsqueeze(-1)
1583	    log_seq_importance_ratio = torch.clamp(log_seq_importance_ratio, max=10.0)  # clamp for numerical stability
1584	
1585	    # finaly exp() to remove log
1586	    seq_importance_ratio = torch.exp(log_seq_importance_ratio)
1587	
1588	    pg_losses1 = -advantages * seq_importance_ratio
1589	    pg_losses2 = -advantages * torch.clamp(seq_importance_ratio, 1 - clip_ratio_low, 1 + clip_ratio_high)
1590	    pg_losses = torch.maximum(pg_losses1, pg_losses2)
1591	
1592	    # Apply rollout correction weights if provided
1593	    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
1594	        pg_losses = pg_losses * rollout_is_weights
1595	
1596	    # for GSPO, we need to aggregate the loss at the sequence level (seq-mean-token-mean)
1597	    pg_loss = agg_loss(
1598	        loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode="seq-mean-token-mean", **config.global_batch_info
1599	    )
1600	
1601	    # For compatibility, return zero for pg_clipfrac_lower (not used in standard GSPO)
1602	    pg_clipfrac = verl_F.masked_mean(torch.gt(pg_losses2, pg_losses1).float(), response_mask)
1603	    pg_clipfrac_lower = torch.tensor(0.0, device=pg_loss.device)
1604	
1605	    ppo_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)
1606	    pg_metrics = {
1607	        "actor/pg_clipfrac": pg_clipfrac.detach().item(),
1608	        "actor/ppo_kl": ppo_kl.detach().item(),
1609	        "actor/pg_clipfrac_lower": pg_clipfrac_lower.detach().item(),
1610	    }
1611	    return pg_loss, pg_metrics

1614	@register_policy_loss("sapo")
1615	def compute_policy_loss_sapo(
1616	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1617	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1618	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
1619	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
1620	    loss_agg_mode: str = "seq-mean-token-mean",
1621	    config: Optional[ActorConfig] = None,
1622	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor | None = None,
1623	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]]:
1624	    """
1625	    Compute the smoothed policy objective and related metrics for SAPO.
1626	
1627	    See https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.20347 for more details.
1628	
1629	    Args:
1630	        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1631	            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1632	        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1633	            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1634	        advantages (torch.Tensor):
1635	            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1636	        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
1637	            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1638	        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
1639	            Aggregation mode for `agg_loss`. For SAPO, it is recommended to use "seq-mean-token-mean".
1640	    """
1641	
1642	    assert config is not None
1643	    assert isinstance(config, ActorConfig)
1644	
1645	    # temperature for positive and negative token updates
1646	    tau_pos = torch.as_tensor(config.tau_pos, dtype=advantages.dtype, device=advantages.device)
1647	    tau_neg = torch.as_tensor(config.tau_neg, dtype=advantages.dtype, device=advantages.device)
1648	
1649	    def gate_function(x, tau):
1650	        """The gating function used in SAPO"""
1651	        return torch.sigmoid(tau * (x - 1.0)) * (4.0 / tau)
1652	
1653	    # compute IS at token level:
1654	    # r_{i,t}(θ) = π_θ(y_{i,t}|x, y_{i,<t}) / π_θold(y_{i,t}|x, y_{i,<t})]
1655	    # In log space: log(r_{i,t}(θ)) = log_prob - ol_log_prob
1656	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
1657	    # Clamp negative_approx_kl for stability
1658	    negative_approx_kl = torch.clamp(negative_approx_kl, min=-20.0, max=20.0)
1659	    # finally exp() to remove log and get r_{i,t}(θ)
1660	    ratio = torch.exp(negative_approx_kl)
1661	
1662	    # tau_{i,t} is tau_pos if adv > 0 else tau_neg
1663	    taus = torch.where(
1664	        condition=advantages > 0,
1665	        input=tau_pos,  # if A_{i,t} > 0 we set to tau_pos
1666	        other=tau_neg,  # if A_{i,t} <= 0 we set to tau_neg
1667	    )
1668	
1669	    # compute the gates f_{i,t}(r_{i,t}(θ)) at token level
1670	    gates = gate_function(ratio, taus)
1671	
1672	    # compute policy gradient loss
1673	    pg_losses = -gates * advantages
1674	
1675	    # Apply rollout correction weights if provided
1676	    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
1677	        pg_losses = pg_losses * rollout_is_weights
1678	
1679	    # for SAPO, we need to aggregate the loss at the sequence level (seq-mean-token-mean)
1680	    pg_loss = agg_loss(
1681	        loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode="seq-mean-token-mean", **config.global_batch_info
1682	    )
1683	
1684	    # For compatibility, return zero for both pg_clipfrac and pg_clipfrac_lower (not used in SAPO)
1685	    pg_clipfrac = torch.tensor(0.0, device=pg_loss.device)
1686	    pg_clipfrac_lower = torch.tensor(0.0, device=pg_loss.device)
1687	    # compute KL for metrics tracking
1688	    ppo_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)
1689	    # return metrics dict
1690	    pg_metrics = {
1691	        "actor/pg_clipfrac": pg_clipfrac.detach().item(),
1692	        "actor/ppo_kl": ppo_kl.detach().item(),
1693	        "actor/pg_clipfrac_lower": pg_clipfrac_lower.detach().item(),
1694	    }
1695	
1696	    return pg_loss, pg_metrics

1735	@register_policy_loss("clip_cov")
1736	def compute_policy_loss_clip_cov(
1737	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1738	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1739	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
1740	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
1741	    loss_agg_mode: str = "token-mean",
1742	    config: Optional[ActorConfig] = None,
1743	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor | None = None,
1744	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]]:
1745	    """
1746	    Compute the clipped policy objective and related metrics for Clip-Cov.
1747	
1748	    Adapted from
1749	    https://github.com/PRIME-RL/Entropy-Mechanism-of-RL/blob/main/verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py
1750	
1751	    Args:
1752	        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1753	            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1754	        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1755	            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1756	        advantages (torch.Tensor):
1757	            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1758	        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
1759	            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1760	        cliprange (float, optional):
1761	            Clipping parameter ε for standard PPO. See https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347.
1762	            Defaults to None (must be provided).
1763	        cliprange_low (float, optional):
1764	            Lower clip range for dual-clip PPO. Defaults to same as `cliprange`.
1765	        cliprange_high (float, optional):
1766	            Upper clip range for dual-clip PPO. Defaults to same as `cliprange`.
1767	        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
1768	            Aggregation mode for `agg_loss`. Defaults to "token-mean".
1769	        clip_cov_ratio (float, optional):
1770	            Ratio for clipping the covariance. Defaults to 0.0002.
1771	        clip_cov_lb (float, optional):
1772	            Lower bound for clipping covariance. Defaults to 1.0.
1773	        clip_cov_ub (float, optional):
1774	            Upper bound for clipping covariance. Defaults to 5.0.
1775	    """
1776	    assert config is not None
1777	    assert not isinstance(config, AlgoConfig), "passing AlgoConfig not supported yet"
1778	    assert config.policy_loss is not None
1779	
1780	    clip_cov_ratio = config.policy_loss.clip_cov_ratio if config.policy_loss.clip_cov_ratio is not None else 0.0002
1781	    cliprange = config.clip_ratio
1782	    cliprange_low = config.clip_ratio_low if config.clip_ratio_low is not None else cliprange
1783	    cliprange_high = config.clip_ratio_high if config.clip_ratio_high is not None else cliprange
1784	    clip_cov_ub = config.policy_loss.clip_cov_ub if config.policy_loss.clip_cov_ub is not None else 5.0
1785	    clip_cov_lb = config.policy_loss.clip_cov_lb if config.policy_loss.clip_cov_lb is not None else 1.0
1786	
1787	    assert clip_cov_ratio > 0, "clip_ratio should be larger than 0."
1788	
1789	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
1790	    ratio = torch.exp(negative_approx_kl)
1791	    ppo_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)
1792	
1793	    pg_losses1 = -advantages * ratio
1794	
1795	    if cliprange_low is None:
1796	        cliprange_low = cliprange
1797	    if cliprange_high is None:
1798	        cliprange_high = cliprange
1799	
1800	    corr = torch.ones_like(advantages)
1801	    pg_losses2 = -advantages * torch.clamp(ratio, 1 - cliprange_low, 1 + cliprange_high)
1802	    clip_by_origin = (pg_losses2 > pg_losses1) & (response_mask > 0)
1803	
1804	    cov_all = (advantages - verl_F.masked_mean(advantages, response_mask)) * (
1805	        log_prob - verl_F.masked_mean(log_prob.detach(), response_mask)
1806	    )
1807	    cov_all[response_mask == 0] = -torch.inf
1808	    cov_all[clip_by_origin] = -torch.inf
1809	
1810	    clip_num = max(int(clip_cov_ratio * response_mask.sum().item()), 1)
1811	    top_k_idx = (cov_all < clip_cov_ub) & (cov_all > clip_cov_lb) & (response_mask > 0)
1812	    top_k_idx = torch.nonzero(top_k_idx)
1813	
1814	    if len(top_k_idx) > 0:
1815	        perm = torch.randperm(len(top_k_idx))
1816	        top_k_idx = top_k_idx[perm[: min(clip_num, len(top_k_idx))]]
1817	    else:
1818	        top_k_idx = torch.empty((0, 2), device=cov_all.device, dtype=torch.long)
1819	
1820	    corr[top_k_idx[:, 0], top_k_idx[:, 1]] = 0
1821	
1822	    pg_clipfrac = verl_F.masked_mean((corr == 0).float(), response_mask)
1823	
1824	    pg_losses = torch.maximum(pg_losses1, pg_losses2) * corr
1825	
1826	    # Apply rollout correction weights if provided
1827	    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
1828	        pg_losses = pg_losses * rollout_is_weights
1829	
1830	    pg_loss = agg_loss(
1831	        loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
1832	    )
1833	    pg_metrics = {
1834	        "actor/pg_clipfrac": pg_clipfrac.detach().item(),
1835	        "actor/ppo_kl": ppo_kl.detach().item(),
1836	    }
1837	    return pg_loss, pg_metrics
1838

1840	@register_policy_loss("kl_cov")
1841	def compute_policy_loss_kl_cov(
1842	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1843	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1844	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
1845	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
1846	    loss_agg_mode: str = "token-mean",
1847	    config: Optional[ActorConfig] = None,
1848	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor | None = None,
1849	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]]:
1850	    """
1851	    Compute the clipped policy objective and related metrics for Clip-Cov.
1852	
1853	    Adapted from
1854	    https://github.com/PRIME-RL/Entropy-Mechanism-of-RL/blob/main/verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py
1855	
1856	    Args:
1857	        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1858	            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1859	        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1860	            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1861	        advantages (torch.Tensor):
1862	            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1863	        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
1864	            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1865	        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
1866	            Aggregation mode for `agg_loss`. Defaults to "token-mean".
1867	        kl_cov_ratio (float, optional):
1868	            Ratio for selecting the top-k covariance values. Defaults to 0.0002.
1869	        ppo_kl_coef (float, optional):
1870	            Coefficient for the KL penalty term in the loss. Defaults to 1.
1871	    """
1872	    assert config is not None
1873	    assert not isinstance(config, AlgoConfig), "passing AlgoConfig not supported yet"
1874	    assert config.policy_loss is not None
1875	
1876	    kl_cov_ratio = config.policy_loss.kl_cov_ratio if config.policy_loss.kl_cov_ratio is not None else 0.0002
1877	    ppo_kl_coef = config.policy_loss.ppo_kl_coef if config.policy_loss.ppo_kl_coef is not None else 1.0
1878	
1879	    assert kl_cov_ratio > 0, "kl_cov_ratio should be larger than 0."
1880	
1881	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
1882	    abs_kl = negative_approx_kl.abs()
1883	    ratio = torch.exp(negative_approx_kl)
1884	    ppo_kl_abs = verl_F.masked_mean(negative_approx_kl.abs(), response_mask)
1885	    pg_losses1 = -advantages * ratio
1886	    pg_losses_kl = -advantages * ratio + ppo_kl_coef * abs_kl
1887	    pg_losses = pg_losses1
1888	
1889	    all_valid = response_mask > 0
1890	    all_valid_idx = torch.nonzero(all_valid.reshape(-1), as_tuple=True)[0]
1891	    all_valid_adv = advantages[all_valid].detach().reshape(-1).cpu()
1892	    all_valid_logp = log_prob[all_valid].detach().reshape(-1).cpu()
1893	
1894	    k = min(kl_cov_ratio, len(all_valid_adv))
1895	
1896	    if k != 0:
1897	        cov_lst_all = (all_valid_adv - all_valid_adv.mean()) * (all_valid_logp - all_valid_logp.mean())
1898	        k_percent_nums = max(1, int(len(cov_lst_all) * kl_cov_ratio))
1899	        large_cov_idxs = torch.topk(cov_lst_all, k_percent_nums, largest=True).indices
1900	
1901	        if len(large_cov_idxs) != 0:
1902	            large_cov_idxs = all_valid_idx[large_cov_idxs]
1903	            pg_losses[large_cov_idxs // advantages.shape[1], large_cov_idxs % advantages.shape[1]] = pg_losses_kl[
1904	                large_cov_idxs // advantages.shape[1], large_cov_idxs % advantages.shape[1]
1905	            ]
1906	
1907	    # Apply rollout correction weights if provided
1908	    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
1909	        pg_losses = pg_losses * rollout_is_weights
1910	
1911	    pg_loss = agg_loss(
1912	        loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
1913	    )
1914	    pg_metrics = {
1915	        "actor/ppo_kl": ppo_kl_abs.detach().item(),
1916	    }
1917	    return pg_loss, pg_metrics
1918

1920	@register_policy_loss("geo_mean")
1921	def compute_policy_loss_geo_mean(
1922	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1923	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1924	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
1925	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
1926	    loss_agg_mode: str = "token-mean",
1927	    config: Optional[ActorConfig] = None,
1928	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor | None = None,
1929	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]]:
1930	    """
1931	    Compute the clipped policy objective and related metrics for GMPO.
1932	
1933	    Adapted from paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.20673
1934	    https://github.com/callsys/GMPO/blob/main/train_zero_math_gmpo.py
1935	
1936	    Args:
1937	        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1938	            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1939	        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1940	            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1941	        advantages (torch.Tensor):
1942	            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1943	        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
1944	            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1945	        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
1946	            not used
1947	    """
1948	
1949	    assert config is not None
1950	    assert not isinstance(config, AlgoConfig)
1951	    clip_ratio = config.clip_ratio  # Clipping parameter. See https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347.
1952	    clip_ratio_low = config.clip_ratio_low if config.clip_ratio_low is not None else clip_ratio
1953	    clip_ratio_high = config.clip_ratio_high if config.clip_ratio_high is not None else clip_ratio
1954	
1955	    cliprange = clip_ratio
1956	    cliprange_low = clip_ratio_low
1957	    cliprange_high = clip_ratio_high
1958	    if cliprange_low is None:
1959	        cliprange_low = cliprange
1960	    if cliprange_high is None:
1961	        cliprange_high = cliprange
1962	
1963	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
1964	    # Clamp negative_approx_kl for stability (uncomment it if you like)
1965	    # negative_approx_kl = torch.clamp(negative_approx_kl, min=-20.0, max=20.0)
1966	    ppo_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)
1967	
1968	    # Clipping at token-level & Clipping wider
1969	    sgn_advantage = torch.sign(advantages)
1970	    negative_approx_kl_clamp = torch.clamp(negative_approx_kl, -cliprange_low, cliprange_high)
1971	    negative_approx_kl_min = torch.min(sgn_advantage * negative_approx_kl, sgn_advantage * negative_approx_kl_clamp)
1972	    negative_approx_kl_min = sgn_advantage * negative_approx_kl_min
1973	
1974	    # Geometric-Mean Policy Optimization
1975	    response_mask_sum = response_mask.sum(dim=-1)
1976	    ratio = torch.exp((negative_approx_kl_min * response_mask).sum(dim=-1) / (response_mask_sum + 1e-8))
1977	    # we only support sequence level advantage for now,
1978	    # otherwise, below would be not consistent with the paper
1979	    advantage = (advantages * response_mask).sum(dim=-1) / (response_mask_sum + 1e-8)
1980	    pg_losses = -advantage * ratio
1981	
1982	    # Apply rollout correction weights if provided
1983	    # For geo_mean, IS weights are 2D (batch_size, seq_length) and need to be aggregated to sequence level
1984	    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
1985	        # Aggregate token-level weights to sequence level using geometric mean for consistency
1986	        # Note: rollout_is_weights is always 2D regardless of aggregation mode
1987	        seq_is_weights = torch.exp(
1988	            (torch.log(rollout_is_weights + 1e-10) * response_mask).sum(dim=-1) / (response_mask_sum + 1e-8)
1989	        )
1990	        pg_losses = pg_losses * seq_is_weights
1991	
1992	    pg_loss = torch.mean(pg_losses)
1993	
1994	    # higher: ratio is too large that need clamp to clip_high (when adv > 0)
1995	    clipped = torch.ne(negative_approx_kl, negative_approx_kl_clamp)
1996	    pg_clipfrac = verl_F.masked_mean((clipped * (advantages > 0)).float(), response_mask)
1997	    pg_clipfrac_lower = verl_F.masked_mean((clipped * (advantages < 0)).float(), response_mask)
1998	    pg_metrics = {
1999	        "actor/pg_clipfrac": pg_clipfrac.detach().item(),
2000	        "actor/ppo_kl": ppo_kl.detach().item(),
2001	        "actor/pg_clipfrac_lower": pg_clipfrac_lower.detach().item(),
2002	    }
2003	    return pg_loss, pg_metrics
2004

2006	@register_policy_loss("cispo")
2007	def compute_policy_loss_cispo(
2008	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
2009	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
2010	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
2011	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
2012	    loss_agg_mode: str = "token-mean",
2013	    config: Optional[DictConfig | ActorConfig] = None,
2014	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor | None = None,
2015	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]]:
2016	    """
2017	    Compute the clipped policy objective and related metrics for CISPO.

2301	    """Compute REINFORCE-style policy gradient loss with optional IS correction.

2304	    sampling correction for rollout-training policy mismatch.
2305	
2306	    Mathematical formulation:
2307	        Without IS (rollout_is_weights=None):
2308	            L = -E[log π(a|s) * A(s,a)]
2309	            Gradient: ∇_θ L = -E[∇log π(a|s) * A] (standard REINFORCE)
2310	
2311	        With IS (rollout_is_weights provided):
2312	            L = -E_π_rollout[w * log π(a|s) * A(s,a)]
2313	            where w = π_current / π_rollout (truncated IS weight)
2314	            Gradient: ∇_θ L = -E[w * ∇log π(a|s) * A] (IS-corrected policy gradient)
2315	
2316	    Args:
2317	        rollout_log_prob: Log probabilities from rollout policy (e.g., vLLM BF16).
2318	            Shape: (batch_size, seq_length). Used for KL computation.
2319	        log_prob: Log probabilities from current training policy.
2320	            Shape: (batch_size, seq_length)
2321	        advantages: Advantage estimates for each token.
2322	            Shape: (batch_size, seq_length)
2323	        response_mask: Mask indicating valid tokens (1 for valid, 0 for padding).
2324	            Shape: (batch_size, seq_length). Should already include rejection sampling.
2325	        loss_agg_mode: Loss aggregation strategy (see agg_loss for details).
2326	        config: Actor config (required for global_batch_info).
2327	        rollout_is_weights: Pre-computed IS weights (π_current / π_rollout).
2328	            Shape: (batch_size, seq_length). None to disable IS correction.
2329	
2330	    Returns:
2331	        Tuple of (loss, metrics):
2332	            loss: Scalar policy gradient loss
2333	            metrics: Dictionary with "actor/ppo_kl"
2334	
2335	    Note:
2336	        Unlike PPO (compute_policy_loss_vanilla), this function:
2337	        - Does NOT use PPO clipping
2338	        - Uses log π(a|s) directly (not ratio)
2339	        - IS weights are applied as multiplicative factor
2340	    """
2341	    assert config is not None, "ActorConfig must be provided for REINFORCE loss"
2342	
2343	    # Compute pure policy gradient loss with optional IS correction
2344	    # Standard REINFORCE: L = -E[log π(a|s) * A]
2345	    # With IS: L = -E[w * log π(a|s) * A] where w = π_current / π_rollout
2346	    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
2347	        # IS-corrected policy gradient: L = -E[stopgrad(w) · log π · A]
2348	        pg_losses = -advantages * log_prob * rollout_is_weights
2349	    else:
2350	        # Standard REINFORCE: L = -E[log π · A]
2351	        pg_losses = -advantages * log_prob
2352	
2353	    # Aggregate loss
2354	    pg_loss = agg_loss(
2355	        loss_mat=pg_losses,
2356	        loss_mask=response_mask,
2357	        loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode,
2358	        **config.global_batch_info,
2359	    )
2360	
2361	    # Compute KL divergence between current and rollout policy
2362	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - rollout_log_prob
2363	    kl_divergence = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)
2364	
2365	    pg_metrics = {
2366	        "actor/ppo_kl": kl_divergence.detach().item(),
2367	    }
2368	
2369	    return pg_loss, pg_metrics

2373	def compute_policy_loss_bypass_mode(
2374	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
2375	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
2376	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
2377	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
2378	    loss_agg_mode: str = "token-mean",

2383	
2384	    This function is the entry point for bypass mode, where old_log_prob = rollout_log_prob.
2385	    It computes IS weights and rejection masks, then dispatches to either REINFORCE or
2386	    PPO-clip loss based on the loss_type configuration.
2387	
2388	    IMPORTANT - Bypass mode semantics:
2389	        In bypass mode, the trainer sets old_log_prob = rollout_log_prob.
2390	        This means:
2391	        - For REINFORCE: We use IS weights w = π_current / π_rollout explicitly
2392	        - For PPO-clip: The PPO ratio π_current / π_old = π_current / π_rollout
2393	          already incorporates the IS correction through clipping, so we do NOT
2394	          apply additional IS weights (would be double-counting)
2395	
2396	    Loss types:
2397	        - "ppo_clip" (default): PPO clipped objective (compute_policy_loss_vanilla)
2398	            L = -E[min(r*A, clip(r)*A)] where r = π_current / π_rollout
2399	            Note: IS weights are NOT applied (clipping handles the ratio)
2400	        - "reinforce": REINFORCE-style policy gradient with IS correction
2401	            L = -E[w * log π(a|s) * A] where w = π_current / π_rollout
2402	
2403	    Args:
2404	        old_log_prob: In bypass mode, this is actually rollout_log_prob.
2405	            Shape: (batch_size, seq_length)
2406	        log_prob: Current policy log probabilities.
2407	            Shape: (batch_size, seq_length)
2408	        advantages: Advantage estimates.
2409	            Shape: (batch_size, seq_length)
2410	        response_mask: Valid token mask (1=valid, 0=padding).
2411	            Shape: (batch_size, seq_length)
2412	        loss_agg_mode: Loss aggregation mode (passed to underlying loss function).
2413	        config: Actor config containing rollout_correction settings in policy_loss.
2414	        rollout_is_weights: Pre-computed IS weights (ignored, computed internally).
2415	
2416	    Config options (in config.policy_loss.rollout_correction):
2417	        loss_type: "ppo_clip" (default) or "reinforce"
2418	        rollout_is: IS aggregation level ("token", "sequence", or None)
2419	        rollout_is_threshold: Upper threshold for truncating IS weights (default: 2.0)
2420	        rollout_rs: Rejection sampling level (see rollout_corr_helper for supported modes)
2421	        rollout_rs_threshold: Threshold specification for rejection sampling
2422	        rollout_is_batch_normalize: Whether to normalize IS weights to mean=1.0

2427	            metrics: Dictionary with rollout correction metrics and actor/ppo_kl

2433	    # Extract rollout_correction config from policy_loss
2434	    rollout_corr_config = config.policy_loss.get("rollout_correction", None) if hasattr(config, "policy_loss") else None

2440	        )
2441	
2442	    # Extract parameters
2443	    loss_type = rollout_corr_config.get("loss_type", "ppo_clip")
2444	    rollout_is = rollout_corr_config.get("rollout_is", None)
2445	    rollout_is_threshold = rollout_corr_config.get("rollout_is_threshold", 2.0)
2446	    rollout_is_batch_normalize = rollout_corr_config.get("rollout_is_batch_normalize", False)
2447	    rollout_rs = rollout_corr_config.get("rollout_rs", None)
2448	    rollout_rs_threshold = rollout_corr_config.get("rollout_rs_threshold", None)
2449	
2450	    # In bypass mode: old_log_prob IS rollout_log_prob
2451	    rollout_log_prob = old_log_prob
2452	
2453	    # Compute IS weights and rejection mask
2454	    # Note: For PPO-clip, we still compute IS weights for metrics, but don't apply them
2455	    with torch.no_grad():

2457	            compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask(
2458	                old_log_prob=log_prob,  # Current policy (for IS ratio: π_current / π_rollout)
2459	                rollout_log_prob=rollout_log_prob,  # Rollout policy
2460	                response_mask=response_mask,
2461	                rollout_is=rollout_is,
2462	                rollout_is_threshold=rollout_is_threshold,
2463	                rollout_is_batch_normalize=rollout_is_batch_normalize,
2464	                rollout_rs=rollout_rs,
2465	                rollout_rs_threshold=rollout_rs_threshold,
2466	            )
2467	        )
2468	
2469	    # Extract IS weights tensor (or None if disabled)
2470	    computed_is_weights = rollout_is_weights_proto.batch["rollout_is_weights"] if rollout_is_weights_proto else None
2471	
2472	    # Apply rejection mask (RS + veto)

steps.reasoning_content:
The config uses vanilla loss mode, grpo adv estimator, kl_loss_type low_var_kl, use_kl_loss true, kl_loss_coef 0.001. Rollout correction disabled (rollout_is: null, rollout_rs: null).

Now let me look for the KL loss application in the actor worker — where kl_penalty is used. In vanilla verl, `compute_kl_loss` uses `kl_penalty(logprob, ref_log_prob, kl_loss_type)` and the actor's KL direction: `old_log_prob - ref_log_prob`... Let me check. In stock verl, `compute_kl_loss` in fsdp_workers or actors. Let me search.

Also I noticed important suspicious points already:
1. In `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage`, `id2std` uses `torch.std` (unbiased, N-1) — fine, matches stock verl.
2. Group size: rollout n=4, train_batch_size=4, ppo_mini_batch_size=4. GRPO groups of 4.

Now key: entropy fell, response lengths saturated. Need to look at where advantage computed — in ray_trainer.py there's `compute_advantage`. Also check `compute_kl_loss` for direction, and megatron actor (this run uses megatron) — the actor update. Let me look at the KL loss code and how advantages are passed.

Also the question mentions advantages all zero -> pg_loss 0. With GRPO, if all scores within a group are equal (all zero reward — collapse), advantages are zero. That's expected consequence, not cause. But the cause might be: KL direction wrong pushing away from ref, entropy collapse, length saturation.

Also check `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage` when use_kl_in_reward false — fine.

Also note in `compute_policy_loss_vanilla`: `pg_losses = torch.where(advantages < 0, clip_pg_losses2, clip_pg_losses1)` — standard dual-clip. Fine.

But wait — `rollout_is_weights` param named `rollout_log_probs` in docstring. In vanilla loss, `pg_losses = pg_losses * rollout_is_weights` — applied for non-bypass loss modes. Where do IS weights get passed for vanilla mode? Check the actor worker code — maybe IS weights are applied by default somewhere even when rollout_correction disabled. Config: rollout_is: null. Need to check where rollout_is_weights enters the actor loss — maybe computed unconditionally in the megatron actor.

Let me look at the KL loss and actors.

88	        fields.append("rollout_is_weights")
89	    if "ref_log_prob" in data:
90	        fields.append("ref_log_prob")
91	    data = data.select(*fields).to_padded_tensor()
92	
93	    response_mask = data["response_mask"].to(bool)
94	    # compute policy loss
95	    old_log_prob = data["old_log_probs"]
96	    advantages = data["advantages"]
97	    rollout_is_weights = data.get("rollout_is_weights", None)
98	
99	    loss_agg_mode = config.loss_agg_mode
100	
101	    loss_mode = config.policy_loss.get("loss_mode", "vanilla")
102	
103	    policy_loss_fn = get_policy_loss_fn(loss_mode)
104	    pg_loss, pg_metrics = policy_loss_fn(
105	        old_log_prob=old_log_prob,
106	        log_prob=log_prob,
107	        advantages=advantages,
108	        response_mask=response_mask,
109	        loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode,
110	        config=config,
111	        rollout_is_weights=rollout_is_weights,
112	    )
113	
114	    # AggregationType.MEAN for pg metrics: assumes policy_loss_fn normalizes by local_bsz/local_tokens
115	    # Ex: in compute_policy_loss_vanilla, pg_metrics are pg_clipfrac, ppo_kl, pg_clipfrac_lower
116	    pg_metrics = Metric.from_dict(pg_metrics, aggregation=AggregationType.MEAN)
117	
118	    metrics.update(pg_metrics)
119	    metrics["actor/pg_loss"] = Metric(value=pg_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)
120	    policy_loss = pg_loss
121	
122	    # add entropy loss
123	    if entropy is not None:
124	        entropy_loss = agg_loss(
125	            loss_mat=entropy, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
126	        )
127	        entropy_coeff = config.entropy_coeff
128	        policy_loss -= entropy_coeff * entropy_loss
129	        metrics["actor/entropy_loss"] = Metric(value=entropy_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)
130	
131	    # add kl loss
132	    if config.use_kl_loss:
133	        ref_log_prob = data["ref_log_prob"]
134	        # compute kl loss
135	        kld = kl_penalty(logprob=log_prob, ref_logprob=ref_log_prob, kl_penalty=config.kl_loss_type)
136	        kl_loss = agg_loss(
137	            loss_mat=kld, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=config.loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
138	        )
139	
140	        policy_loss += kl_loss * config.kl_loss_coef
141	        metrics["kl_loss"] = Metric(value=kl_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)
142	        metrics["kl_coef"] = config.kl_loss_coef
143	
144	    return policy_loss, metrics

146	
147	def value_loss(config: CriticConfig, model_output, data: TensorDict, dp_group=None):
148	    """value loss
149	
150	    Args:
151	        config: CriticConfig
152	        model_output: model output from the model
153	        data: the input to the model
154	        dp_group: data paralle group
155	
156	    Returns:
157	        value loss
158	    """
159	    vpreds = no_padding_2_padding(model_output["values"], data)  # (bsz, response_length)
160	
161	    # Normalize the value loss over the global mini-batch (dp_size / batch_num_tokens /
162	    # global_batch_size) instead of the local micro-batch, so the accumulated critic gradient is
163	    # invariant to how the mini-batch is split into micro-batches (as the actor's ppo_loss does).
164	    dp_size = data["dp_size"]
165	    batch_num_tokens = data["batch_num_tokens"]
166	    global_batch_size = data["global_batch_size"]
167	
168	    # When the loss is normalized over the global batch, each micro-batch contributes a partial sum,
169	    # so the loss metric must be aggregated with SUM to reflect the global-batch mean.
170	    if (
171	        dp_size > 1
172	        or batch_num_tokens is not None
173	        or global_batch_size is not None
174	        or config.loss_scale_factor is not None
175	    ):
176	        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.SUM
177	    else:
178	        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.MEAN
179	
180	    # select fields and convert to padded tensor
181	    data = data.select("values", "returns", "response_mask").to_padded_tensor()
182	    values = data["values"]
183	    returns = data["returns"]
184	    response_mask = data["response_mask"].to(bool)
185	
186	    vf_loss, vf_clipfrac = compute_value_loss(
187	        vpreds=vpreds,
188	        values=values,
189	        returns=returns,
190	        response_mask=response_mask,
191	        cliprange_value=config.cliprange_value,
192	        loss_agg_mode=config.loss_agg_mode,
193	        dp_size=dp_size,
194	        batch_num_tokens=batch_num_tokens,
195	        global_batch_size=global_batch_size,
196	        loss_scale_factor=config.loss_scale_factor,
197	    )
198	
199	    metrics = {
200	        "critic/vf_loss": Metric(value=vf_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation),
201	        "critic/vf_clipfrac": vf_clipfrac.detach().item(),
202	        "critic/vpred_mean": masked_mean(vpreds, response_mask).detach().item(),
203	    }
204	
205	    return vf_loss, metrics

# GPU wiring for the Harbor backend.
#
# The native docker runtime translates metadata.environment.env's
# NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES into `--gpus` itself (ptdbench/runtimes/providers/
# docker.py::_gpu_args). Harbor's path has no equivalent: the generated
# task.toml carries no `gpus` field, and harbor's local docker environment
# reports `gpus: False` in its capabilities, so even asking for GPUs there is
# rejected. What harbor *does* honour is a task-authored compose override on
# the `main` service, merged after its own build/prebuilt compose
# (harbor/src/harbor/environments/docker/docker.py::_docker_compose_paths).
# The harbor adapter passes this file to `harbor run --extra-docker-compose`
# (ptdbench/evaluation/harbor_evaluator.py::HarborRunner._compose_overlay_args);
# it cannot go into the generated task's environment/, because harbor stops
# uploading the workspace from there once a compose file is present.
#
# This file is inert on the native docker path -- nothing there reads compose.
services:
  main:
    # ray + sglang pass tensors between workers through /dev/shm and NCCL opens
    # its buffers there. Docker's 64MB default dies on the first rollout with an
    # opaque bus error. Same value as DEFAULT_SHM_SIZE in the docker runtime.
    shm_size: "16gb"
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: all
              capabilities: [gpu]

# GPU wiring for the Harbor backend.
#
# The native docker runtime translates metadata.environment.env's
# NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES into `--gpus` itself (ptdbench/runtimes/providers/
# docker.py::_gpu_args). Harbor's path has no equivalent: the generated
# task.toml carries no `gpus` field, and harbor's local docker environment
# reports `gpus: False` in its capabilities, so even asking for GPUs there is
# rejected. What harbor *does* honour is a task-authored compose override on
# the `main` service, merged after its own build/prebuilt compose
# (harbor/src/harbor/environments/docker/docker.py::_docker_compose_paths).
# The harbor adapter passes this file to `harbor run --extra-docker-compose`
# (ptdbench/evaluation/harbor_evaluator.py::HarborRunner._compose_overlay_args);
# it cannot go into the generated task's environment/, because harbor stops
# uploading the workspace from there once a compose file is present.
#
# This file is inert on the native docker path -- nothing there reads compose.
services:
  main:
    # ray + sglang pass tensors between workers through /dev/shm and NCCL opens
    # its buffers there. Docker's 64MB default dies on the first rollout with an
    # opaque bus error. Same value as DEFAULT_SHM_SIZE in the docker runtime.
    shm_size: "16gb"
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: all
              capabilities: [gpu]

14	"""Utils for tokenization."""
15	
16	import types
17	import warnings
18	
19	__all__ = [
20	    "hf_tokenizer",
21	    "hf_processor",
22	    "normalize_token_ids",
23	    "build_multimodal_processor_inputs",
24	    "get_processor_token_id",
25	]
26	
27	
28	def normalize_token_ids(tokenized_output) -> list[int]:
29	    """Normalize tokenizer outputs into a flat ``list[int]``.
30	
31	    This handles Transformers 4/5 differences where ``apply_chat_template(tokenize=True)``
32	    may return either ``list[int]`` or a ``BatchEncoding``/mapping with ``input_ids``.
33	    """
34	
35	    token_ids = tokenized_output
36	    if isinstance(tokenized_output, dict):
37	        if "input_ids" in tokenized_output:
38	            token_ids = tokenized_output["input_ids"]
39	    elif hasattr(tokenized_output, "input_ids"):
40	        token_ids = tokenized_output.input_ids
41	
42	    if hasattr(token_ids, "tolist"):
43	        token_ids = token_ids.tolist()
44	
45	    if isinstance(token_ids, tuple):
46	        token_ids = list(token_ids)
47	
48	    if isinstance(token_ids, list) and len(token_ids) == 1 and isinstance(token_ids[0], list | tuple):
49	        token_ids = list(token_ids[0])
50	
51	    if not isinstance(token_ids, list):
52	        raise TypeError(f"token_ids must be list-like token ids, got {type(token_ids).__name__}: {token_ids!r}")
53	
54	    normalized_ids = []
55	    for idx, token_id in enumerate(token_ids):
56	        if hasattr(token_id, "item"):
57	            token_id = token_id.item()
58	        try:
59	            normalized_ids.append(int(token_id))
60	        except (TypeError, ValueError) as e:
61	            raise TypeError(f"token_id must be int-convertible, got {type(token_id).__name__}: {token_id!r}") from e
62	    return normalized_ids
63	
64	
65	def get_processor_token_id(processor, token_name: str) -> int | None:
66	    """Resolve a multimodal special token id from a processor.
67	
68	    Newer processors may expose ``image_token``/``video_token`` strings instead
69	    of ``image_token_id``/``video_token_id`` integers. Fall back to tokenizer
70	    conversion so rollout code can stay processor-agnostic.
71	    """
72	
73	    if processor is None:
74	        return None
75	
76	    token_id_attr = f"{token_name}_token_id"
77	    token_id = getattr(processor, token_id_attr, None)
78	    if token_id is not None:
79	        return int(token_id)
80	
81	    token_attr = f"{token_name}_token"
82	    token = getattr(processor, token_attr, None)
83	    tokenizer = getattr(processor, "tokenizer", None)
84	    if token is not None and tokenizer is not None:
85	        converted = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(token)
86	        if converted is not None:
87	            return int(converted)
88	
89	    return None
90	
91	
92	def _split_videos_and_metadata(videos):
93	    if videos is None:
94	        return None, None
95	    videos = list(videos)
96	    if len(videos) > 0 and isinstance(videos[0], tuple):
97	        video_values, video_metadata = zip(*videos, strict=False)
98	        return list(video_values), list(video_metadata)
99	    return videos, None
100	
101	
102	def build_multimodal_processor_inputs(
103	    processor,
104	    *,
105	    text,
106	    images=None,
107	    videos=None,
108	    audio=None,
109	    mm_processor_kwargs=None,
110	    return_tensors: str = "pt",
111	):
112	    """Build kwargs for multimodal processor calls.
113	
114	    This keeps the existing VL flow intact while extending it with audio-aware
115	    paths for processors that accept audio inputs.
116	    """
117	    processor_kwargs = dict(mm_processor_kwargs or {})
118	    if audio is not None and "sampling_rate" not in processor_kwargs:
119	        sampling_rate = getattr(getattr(processor, "feature_extractor", None), "sampling_rate", None)
120	        if sampling_rate is not None:
121	            processor_kwargs["sampling_rate"] = int(sampling_rate)
122	
123	    videos, video_metadata = _split_videos_and_metadata(videos)
124	    processor_kwargs.setdefault("return_tensors", return_tensors)
125	
126	    if video_metadata is not None:
127	        processor_kwargs.setdefault("video_metadata", video_metadata)
128	        processor_kwargs.setdefault("do_sample_frames", False)
129	
130	    processor_inputs = {"text": text, "images": images, "videos": videos, **processor_kwargs}
131	    if audio is not None:
132	        processor_inputs["audio"] = audio
133	
134	    return processor(**processor_inputs)
135	
136	
137	def set_pad_token_id(tokenizer):
138	    """Set pad_token_id to eos_token_id if it is None.
139	
140	    Args:
141	        tokenizer (transformers.PreTrainedTokenizer): The tokenizer to be set.
142	
143	    """
144	    if tokenizer.pad_token_id is None:
145	        tokenizer.pad_token_id = tokenizer.eos_token_id
146	        warnings.warn(f"tokenizer.pad_token_id is None. Now set to {tokenizer.eos_token_id}", stacklevel=1)
147	    if tokenizer.pad_token is None:
148	        tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token
149	        warnings.warn(f"tokenizer.pad_token is None. Now set to {tokenizer.eos_token}", stacklevel=1)
150	
151	
152	def hf_tokenizer(name_or_path, correct_pad_token=True, correct_gemma2=True, **kwargs):
153	    """Create a huggingface pretrained tokenizer which correctness handles eos and pad tokens.
154	
155	    Args:
156	
157	        name (str): The name of the tokenizer.
158	        correct_pad_token (bool): Whether to correct the pad token id.
159	        correct_gemma2 (bool): Whether to correct the gemma2 tokenizer.
160	
161	    Returns:
162	
163	        transformers.PreTrainedTokenizer: The pretrained tokenizer.
164	
165	    """
166	    from transformers import AutoTokenizer
167	
168	    if correct_gemma2 and isinstance(name_or_path, str) and "gemma-2-2b-it" in name_or_path:
169	        # the EOS token in gemma2 is ambiguious, which may worsen RL performance.
170	        # https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-2-2b-it/commit/17a01657f5c87135bcdd0ec7abb4b2dece04408a
171	        warnings.warn(
172	            "Found gemma-2-2b-it tokenizer. Set eos_token and eos_token_id to <end_of_turn> and 107.", stacklevel=1
173	        )
174	        kwargs["eos_token"] = "<end_of_turn>"
175	        kwargs["eos_token_id"] = 107
176	    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name_or_path, **kwargs)
177	    if correct_pad_token:
178	        set_pad_token_id(tokenizer)
179	    return tokenizer
180	
181	
182	def hf_processor(name_or_path, **kwargs):
183	    """Create a huggingface processor to process multimodal data.
184	
185	    Args:
186	        name_or_path (str): The name of the processor.
187	
188	    Returns:
189	        Optional[transformers.ProcessorMixin]: The pretrained multimodal processor.
190	        Returns ``None`` for text-only models (including AutoProcessor fallbacks to
191	        tokenizer backends such as ``TokenizersBackend``).
192	    """
193	    from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoProcessor, PreTrainedTokenizerBase
194	
195	    try:
196	        processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(name_or_path, **kwargs)
197	        # In newer transformers, AutoProcessor may legitimately fall back to a
198	        # tokenizer backend (e.g. TokenizersBackend) for text-only models.
199	        # Treat it as "no multimodal processor" and let callers use hf_tokenizer.
200	        if isinstance(processor, PreTrainedTokenizerBase):
201	            return None
202	
203	        config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(name_or_path, **kwargs)
204	
205	        # Bind vlm model's get_rope_index method to processor.
206	        processor.config = config
207	        model_class = None
208	        match processor.__class__.__name__:
209	            case "Qwen2VLProcessor":
210	                from transformers.models.qwen2_vl import Qwen2VLModel
211	
212	                model_class = Qwen2VLModel
213	            case "Qwen2_5_VLProcessor":
214	                from transformers.models.qwen2_5_vl import Qwen2_5_VLModel
215	
216	                model_class = Qwen2_5_VLModel
