57	def ppo_loss(config: ActorConfig, model_output, data: TensorDict, dp_group=None):
58	    """Computes ppo loss from model output (log_prob, entropy, values, etc. ) and old_log_probs from data."""
59	    log_prob = no_padding_2_padding(model_output["log_probs"], data)
60	    entropy = model_output.get("entropy", None)
61	    if entropy is not None:
62	        entropy = no_padding_2_padding(entropy, data)
63	
64	    # global batch info for loss aggregation
65	    config.global_batch_info["dp_size"] = data["dp_size"]
66	    config.global_batch_info["batch_num_tokens"] = data["batch_num_tokens"]
67	    config.global_batch_info["global_batch_size"] = data["global_batch_size"]
68	    config.global_batch_info["loss_scale_factor"] = config.loss_scale_factor
69	
70	    # assumes that if any of the global batch info is set, the policy_loss_fn will
71	    # normalize using dp_size/global_bsz/global_token; in this case, metric aggregation should be SUM
72	    # to reflect the mean loss over the global batch
73	    if (
74	        data["dp_size"] > 1
75	        or data["batch_num_tokens"] is not None
76	        or data["global_batch_size"] is not None
77	        or config.loss_scale_factor is not None
78	    ):
79	        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.SUM
80	    else:
81	        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.MEAN
82	
83	    metrics = {}
84	
85	    # select fields and convert to padded tensor
86	    fields = ["response_mask", "old_log_probs", "advantages"]
87	    if "rollout_is_weights" in data:
88	        fields.append("rollout_is_weights")
89	    if "ref_log_prob" in data:
90	        fields.append("ref_log_prob")
91	    data = data.select(*fields).to_padded_tensor()
92	
93	    response_mask = data["response_mask"].to(bool)
94	    # compute policy loss
95	    old_log_prob = data["old_log_probs"]
96	    advantages = data["advantages"]
97	    rollout_is_weights = data.get("rollout_is_weights", None)
98	
99	    loss_agg_mode = config.loss_agg_mode
100	
101	    loss_mode = config.policy_loss.get("loss_mode", "vanilla")
102	
103	    policy_loss_fn = get_policy_loss_fn(loss_mode)
104	    pg_loss, pg_metrics = policy_loss_fn(
105	        old_log_prob=old_log_prob,
106	        log_prob=log_prob,
107	        advantages=advantages,
108	        response_mask=response_mask,
109	        loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode,
110	        config=config,
111	        rollout_is_weights=rollout_is_weights,
112	    )
113	
114	    # AggregationType.MEAN for pg metrics: assumes policy_loss_fn normalizes by local_bsz/local_tokens
115	    # Ex: in compute_policy_loss_vanilla, pg_metrics are pg_clipfrac, ppo_kl, pg_clipfrac_lower
116	    pg_metrics = Metric.from_dict(pg_metrics, aggregation=AggregationType.MEAN)
117	
118	    metrics.update(pg_metrics)
119	    metrics["actor/pg_loss"] = Metric(value=pg_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)
120	    policy_loss = pg_loss
121	
122	    # add entropy loss
123	    if entropy is not None:
124	        entropy_loss = agg_loss(
125	            loss_mat=entropy, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
126	        )
127	        entropy_coeff = config.entropy_coeff
128	        policy_loss -= entropy_coeff * entropy_loss
129	        metrics["actor/entropy_loss"] = Metric(value=entropy_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)
130	
131	    # add kl loss
132	    if config.use_kl_loss:
133	        ref_log_prob = data["ref_log_prob"]
134	        # compute kl loss
135	        kld = kl_penalty(logprob=log_prob, ref_logprob=ref_log_prob, kl_penalty=config.kl_loss_type)
136	        kl_loss = agg_loss(
137	            loss_mat=kld, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=config.loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
138	        )
139	
140	        policy_loss += kl_loss * config.kl_loss_coef
141	        metrics["kl_loss"] = Metric(value=kl_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)
142	        metrics["kl_coef"] = config.kl_loss_coef
143	
144	    return policy_loss, metrics

147	def value_loss(config: CriticConfig, model_output, data: TensorDict, dp_group=None):
148	    """value loss
149	
150	    Args:
151	        config: CriticConfig
152	        model_output: model output from the model
153	        data: the input to the model
154	        dp_group: data paralle group
155	
156	    Returns:
157	        value loss

159	    vpreds = no_padding_2_padding(model_output["values"], data)  # (bsz, response_length)
160	
161	    # Normalize the value loss over the global mini-batch (dp_size / batch_num_tokens /
162	    # global_batch_size) instead of the local micro-batch, so the accumulated critic gradient is
163	    # invariant to how the mini-batch is split into micro-batches (as the actor's ppo_loss does).
164	    dp_size = data["dp_size"]
165	    batch_num_tokens = data["batch_num_tokens"]
166	    global_batch_size = data["global_batch_size"]
167	
168	    # When the loss is normalized over the global batch, each micro-batch contributes a partial sum,
169	    # so the loss metric must be aggregated with SUM to reflect the global-batch mean.
170	    if (
171	        dp_size > 1
172	        or batch_num_tokens is not None
173	        or global_batch_size is not None
174	        or config.loss_scale_factor is not None
175	    ):
176	        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.SUM
177	    else:
178	        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.MEAN
179	
180	    # select fields and convert to padded tensor
181	    data = data.select("values", "returns", "response_mask").to_padded_tensor()
182	    values = data["values"]
183	    returns = data["returns"]
184	    response_mask = data["response_mask"].to(bool)
185	
186	    vf_loss, vf_clipfrac = compute_value_loss(
187	        vpreds=vpreds,
188	        values=values,
189	        returns=returns,
190	        response_mask=response_mask,
191	        cliprange_value=config.cliprange_value,
192	        loss_agg_mode=config.loss_agg_mode,
193	        dp_size=dp_size,
194	        batch_num_tokens=batch_num_tokens,
195	        global_batch_size=global_batch_size,
196	        loss_scale_factor=config.loss_scale_factor,
197	    )
198	
199	    metrics = {
200	        "critic/vf_loss": Metric(value=vf_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation),
201	        "critic/vf_clipfrac": vf_clipfrac.detach().item(),
202	        "critic/vpred_mean": masked_mean(vpreds, response_mask).detach().item(),
203	    }
204	
205	    return vf_loss, metrics

266	# NOTE(sgm): this implementation only consider outcome supervision, where the reward is a scalar.
267	@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GRPO)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("grpo")
268	def compute_grpo_outcome_advantage(
269	    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
270	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
271	    index: np.ndarray,
272	    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
273	    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
274	    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
275	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
276	    """
277	    Compute advantage for GRPO, operating only on Outcome reward
278	    (with only one scalar reward for each response).
279	
280	    Args:
281	        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
282	            shape is (bs, response_length)
283	        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
284	            shape is (bs, response_length)
285	        index: `(np.ndarray)`
286	            index array for grouping
287	        epsilon: `(float)`
288	            small value to avoid division by zero
289	        norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: `(bool)`
290	            whether to scale the GRPO advantage
291	        config: `(Optional[AlgoConfig])`
292	            algorithm configuration object
293	
294	    Note:
295	        If norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo is True, the advantage is scaled by the std, as in the original GRPO.
296	        If False, the advantage is not scaled, as in Dr.GRPO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783).
297	
298	    Returns:
299	        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
300	            shape is (bs, response_length)
301	        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
302	            shape is (bs, response_length)
303	    """
304	    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)
305	
306	    id2score = defaultdict(list)
307	    id2mean = {}
308	    id2std = {}
309	
310	    with torch.no_grad():
311	        bsz = scores.shape[0]
312	        for i in range(bsz):
313	            id2score[index[i]].append(scores[i])
314	        for idx in id2score:
315	            if len(id2score[idx]) == 1:
316	                id2mean[idx] = torch.tensor(0.0)
317	                id2std[idx] = torch.tensor(1.0)
318	            elif len(id2score[idx]) > 1:
319	                scores_tensor = torch.stack(id2score[idx])
320	                id2mean[idx] = torch.mean(scores_tensor)
321	                id2std[idx] = torch.std(scores_tensor)
322	            else:
323	                raise ValueError(f"no score in prompt index: {idx}")
324	        for i in range(bsz):
325	            if norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo:
326	                scores[i] = (scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]) / (id2std[index[i]] + epsilon)
327	            else:
328	                scores[i] = scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]
329	        scores = scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask
330	
331	    return scores, scores

steps.message: The rollout agent's partial output shows `extra_info` including `temperature` and `actor.shuffle` being set somewhere in the trainer. If `old_log_probs` (recomputed) and the training `log_prob` treat temperature differently, the importance ratio is systematically biased. Let me trace where `temperature` in `extra_info` is consumed.
steps.reasoning_content:
The GRPO advantage and vanilla loss are standard verl. Now the remaining deep-dive: the entropy metric and the actor's `ppo_epochs` / mini-batch update loop; and the `compute_old_log_prob` path in ray_trainer. Also the response_mask includes EOS. Let me look at ray_trainer's fit-loop update section and `_compute_old_log_prob` more carefully, plus the `actor_rollout_ref` worker.

Also, importantly: there's an actor entropy metric (falling). And `actor/kl_loss` metric — the kl_loss metric reported by losses.py at line 141. It went 0.003 → 0.7. Since pg_loss = 0 (all advantages zero), the only gradient is 0.001 * kl grad. That can't push KL to 0.7. So KL rose BEFORE advantages collapsed. With clip_ratio 0.2 and ratio clipping, KL between old and new per update is bounded-ish, but KL to REF accumulates over 150 steps.

Hmm — actually wait. Something important: `old_log_prob` recompute — `rollout.calculate_log_probs: true` means the rollout engine (vLLM) computes rollout_log_probs. And then `_compute_old_log_prob` recomputes old_log_probs with the actor (HF/Megatron model). If the vLLM weights are out of sync with actor weights, rollout_log_probs ≠ actor log_probs — but old_log_probs is recomputed by the actor so IS weights are consistent. The metrics path uses rollout_log_probs for off-policy metrics only. OK.

Now, let me think about "what drives long degenerate outputs". One classic injected bug: masking response_mask incorrectly (e.g., shifting). We verified get_response_mask counts up to and including EOS. no_padding_2_padding left-shifts by 1 (line 139-140: `values[seq_offset - resp_len - 1 : seq_offset - 1]`) — that's correct alignment for log probs of response tokens.

Another classic: the position_ids / attention mask for training vs rollout mismatch (e.g., prompt left-padding handled wrong) — the rollout agent might catch it.

Another: `dynamic_bsz` with `ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu: 1536` — micro-batches packed by token length. With max_response 1024 + prompt up to 512, sequences are ~1536. use_dynamic_bsz: true, ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu: 1536. That's normal.

Let me now look at the actor update loop in ray_trainer (fit) and specifically the `update_actor` / ppo_mini_batch_size handling to check for mini-batch / epoch issues, and importantly the **old_log_prob update across epochs**: verl computes old_log_probs once per batch, then runs `ppo_epochs` (default 1) — fine.

vLLM 0.17.0 is installed locally. This is very important: in vLLM, SamplingParams temperature=0 → greedy. In SamplingParams there's a validation: temperature must be positive... Actually in vLLM, when temperature is 0, greedy sampling is used. In older vLLM there was a deprecation: temperature=0 with top_p/top_k... In vLLM 0.17, `SamplingParams` has `temperature: float = 1.0`, and if temperature == 0 then greedy is applied (it sets `_verify_args` maybe warns if top_p != 1 or top_k != -1 with temperature 0). Fine.

Key question: the default val_kwargs in yaml: top_k=-1, top_p=1.0, temperature=0, so validation is greedy by default. The run in question had val_kwargs do_sample=false n=1 — presumably defaults → temperature 0. So validation is greedy. That's fine.

But wait — the user's run set "val_kwargs do_sample=false n=1". If they only specified do_sample and n, then temperature default 0 (from yaml). Good — greedy validation.

Now the interesting big-picture: observed validation accuracy 0.0 at steps 100 and 150, training reward 0 from step 85, response length exactly 1024 clip ratio 1.0. The policy collapsed into non-terminating generations. In GRPO with GSM8K, reward 0 for truncated sequences (no final answer). What in the rollout path could accelerate this?

Important candidate: **the vLLM async server passes sampling params, but temperature=0.8 top_p=0.95 etc. are fine. The repetition_penalty setdefault: agent_loop.py sets repetition_penalty=1.0 in sampling_params (line 576-583 dict), and vllm_async_server line 584 setdefault 1.0 — no effect.**

Another candidate: **override_generation_config** at line ~1021: `max_new_tokens=self.config.response_length` — this overrides the model's HF generation_config including... wait, override_generation_config only overrides the specified keys: temperature, top_k, top_p, repetition_penalty, max_new_tokens. In vLLM, when per-request SamplingParams are provided, they take precedence over generation config defaults. Actually override_generation_config sets engine-level defaults; per-request SamplingParams override them. The agent loop always passes temperature/top_p/top_k, so those are per-request. But **eos handling**: vLLM's stop token determination uses `sampling_params.stop_token_ids` plus the model's generation_config eos_token_id (from HF). `override_generation_config` doesn't remove eos_token_id — the model's generation_config.json is loaded separately. Actually in vLLM, `override_generation_config` merges with the model's generation config, so eos_token_id from the model config remains. OK.

But here's a real potential bug: Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat generation_config.json has eos_token_id = [151645, 151643] (<|im_end|> and <|endoftext|>). vLLM reads that. Fine.

Let me think about what actually causes reward collapse to 0 and never-terminating generations. In GRPO on GSM8K, a classic cause: the model learns to produce long repetitive outputs when there's no length penalty and truncated responses get 0 reward — but that's an RL dynamics issue, not a code bug. The audit's job is to find code bugs.

def _compute_multi_modal_inputs(self, output, input_ids) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """Compute multi-modal inputs with image, video and audio."""
        multi_modal_inputs = {}
        if self.processor is None:
            return multi_modal_inputs

        multi_modal_data = output.multi_modal_data or {}
        images = multi_modal_data.get("images")
        videos = multi_modal_data.get("videos")
        audios = multi_modal_data.get("audios")
        current_text = self.tokenizer.decode(input_ids.squeeze(0), skip_special_tokens=True)

        multi_modal_inputs = build_multimodal_processor_inputs(
            self.processor,
            text=[current_text],
            images=images,
            videos=videos,
            audio=audios,
            mm_processor_kwargs=output.mm_processor_kwargs
            if output.mm_processor_kwargs is not None
            else self._get_mm_processor_kwargs(audios),
        )
        multi_modal_inputs.pop("input_ids", None)
        multi_modal_inputs.pop("attention_mask", None)

        # We must use dict(multi_modal_inputs) to convert BatchFeature values to a new dict
        # because np.array() only keeps the keys for BatchFeature.
        multi_modal_inputs = dict(multi_modal_inputs.convert_to_tensors("pt"))
        image_grid_thw = multi_modal_inputs.get("image_grid_thw")
        if image_grid_thw is not None:
            images_seqlens = torch.repeat_interleave(image_grid_thw[:, 1] * image_grid_thw[:, 2], image_grid_thw[:, 0])
            multi_modal_inputs["images_seqlens"] = images_seqlens
        return multi_modal_inputs

    def _compute_position_ids(
        self,
        input_ids,
        attention_mask,
        multi_modal_inputs,
        mm_processor_kwargs: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Compute position ids for multi-modal inputs."""
        # text-only OR non-M-RoPE multimodal (e.g. Gemma4) -> standard 1D positions
        if self.processor is None or not hasattr(self.processor, "get_rope_index"):
            return compute_position_id_with_mask(attention_mask)  # (1, seq_len)

        multi_modal_kwargs = {
            "image_grid_thw": multi_modal_inputs.get("image_grid_thw"),
            "video_grid_thw": multi_modal_inputs.get("video_grid_thw"),
        }
        # For transformers>=5.3.0, mm_token_type_ids is only used to calculate position ids.
        if multi_modal_inputs.pop("mm_token_type_ids", None) is not None:
            mm_token_type_ids = torch.zeros_like(input_ids)
            image_token_id = get_processor_token_id(self.processor, "image")
            video_token_id = get_processor_token_id(self.processor, "video")
            if image_token_id is not None:
                mm_token_type_ids[0][input_ids[0] == image_token_id] = 1
            if video_token_id is not None:
                mm_token_type_ids[0][input_ids[0] == video_token_id] = 2
            multi_modal_kwargs["mm_token_type_ids"] = mm_token_type_ids

        # Model's get_rope_index has been dynamically bind to the processor.
        vision_position_ids, _ = self.processor.get_rope_index(
            input_ids=input_ids,
            attention_mask=attention_mask,
            **multi_modal_kwargs,
        )
        vision_position_ids = vision_position_ids.transpose(0, 1)  # (3, 1, seq_len) => (1, 3, seq_len)

        valid_mask = attention_mask[0].bool()
        text_position_ids = torch.ones((1, len(input_ids[0])), dtype=torch.long)
        text_position_ids[0, valid_mask] = torch.arange(valid_mask.sum().item())
        text_position_ids = text_position_ids.unsqueeze(0)
        position_ids = torch.cat((text_position_ids, vision_position_ids), dim=1)  # (1, 4, seq_length)
        return position_ids

43	    """Tokens a chat template inserts after a message's closing token, before the next turn.
44	
45	    Multi-turn agent rollouts build the token sequence incrementally. The model stops at the
46	    assistant close token (e.g. ``<|im_end|>``) and never emits the template's trailing
47	    turn-separator (e.g. ``"\\n"``, id 198 for Qwen). Rendering the following tool/user turn in
48	    isolation also omits that separator, so every turn boundary silently drops it and the rollout
49	    token sequence diverges from ``apply_chat_template`` of the equivalent full conversation.
50	    This returns the separator so callers can restore it at turn boundaries.
51	
52	    Derivation: rendering the same (user) turn with empty vs non-empty content only differs in the
53	    content region, so the maximal common trailing run is exactly ``[close_token, *separator]``.
54	    A user turn is used deliberately -- probing with an assistant turn would inject reasoning
55	    scaffolding (e.g. Qwen3's ``<think></think>``) that is not part of the separator. The model
56	    emits the close token itself (it is the stop token), so the separator is everything after it.
57

59	    callers keep their previous behavior instead of crashing.
60	    """

62	    # A bare string ``content`` is rejected by some multimodal processors (they iterate ``content``
63	    # expecting a list of typed parts), so fall back to the list-of-parts form, and return ``[]`` if
64	    # neither renders. Both probes must use the same form so only the body differs.

In Megatron, when `calculate_per_token_loss=True`, the DDP gradient all-reduce does NOT average by world size (no 1/dp division). verl's loss is already normalized over the global batch (token-mean with batch_num_tokens all-reduced), so each rank's loss is already the global mean; summing gradients across DP ranks would multiply by dp_size, hence the division by dp_cp_world_size to compensate.

All verification is complete. The last open item — vLLM per-request EOS application — is confirmed: `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py:292-297` clones each request's SamplingParams and calls `sampling_params.update_from_generation_config(self.generation_config_fields, self.renderer.get_eos_token_id())`, so the model's generation-config EOS is added to the stop set for verl's explicitly constructed params (verl leaves `ignore_eos` False). The rollout path's EOS wiring is sound. Final audit report follows.

---

# Audit report: rollout path of the verl snapshot

Scope: `verl/experimental/agent_loop/{agent_loop,single_turn_agent_loop,tool_agent_loop}.py`, `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/*.py`, `verl/workers/rollout/{schemas,replica,hf_rollout}.py`, trainer generation/validation flow, and the installed vLLM 0.17.0 stop-token internals. All paths below are relative to `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework` unless marked as installed vLLM.

## Executive summary

No bug was found in the rollout path that would *cause* the collapse (wrong EOS ids, tokenizer mismatch, mask mislabeling, off-by-one in log-prob shift, or silently ignored sampling parameters). The EOS/stop machinery is wired correctly end-to-end: vLLM applies the model's generation-config EOS to every request unless `ignore_eos`, which verl defaults to False. The observed symptom — every rollout hitting exactly 1024 tokens with `clip_ratio=1.0`, reward → 0, validation accuracy 0.0 — is policy degeneration under GRPO, not a rollout artifact. However, the rollout path contains several real-but-latent defects and one serious observability defect that *masked* the collapse:

1. **`do_sample=False` for validation is silently ignored** in the agent-loop/vLLM path (real bug, latent — this run was saved only by the YAML default `val_kwargs.temperature: 0`).
2. **finish_reason "stop" and "length" are collapsed** to the same stop_reason, so the trainer cannot distinguish "model emitted EOS" from "truncated" (real observability bug — this is why clip_ratio 1.0 was the only visible symptom).
3. **Edge-case bugs** in `rollout_log_probs` propagation (aborted/zero-token samples can drop the whole batch's bypass log-probs).
4. `num_turns=2` is hardcoded for single-turn (benign, explains the constant num_turns).

Details follow.

---

## 1. Validation greedy decoding: `do_sample=False` is never consumed — REAL BUG (latent; benign for this run)

**Files/lines:**
- `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py:631` — writes `"do_sample": self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample` into `meta_info`.
- `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework/verl/experimental/agent_loop/agent_loop.py:603-607` — validation override:
  ```python
  # override sampling params for validation
  if validate:
      sampling_params["top_p"] = config.val_kwargs.top_p
      sampling_params["top_k"] = config.val_kwargs.top_k
      sampling_params["temperature"] = config.val_kwargs.temperature
  ```
- `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework/verl/experimental/agent_loop/agent_loop.py:598-601` — greedy helper that exists but is only used for REMAX:
  ```python
  def apply_greedy_sampling_params(params: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
      params["top_p"] = 1.0
      params["top_k"] = -1
      params["temperature"] = 0
  ```
  applied only at `agent_loop.py:647-648` under `if not validate and per_sample_do_sample ...`.
- `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework/verl/workers/rollout/hf_rollout.py:56-66` — evidence of intended behavior that was never ported:
  ```python
  do_sample = prompts.meta_info.get("do_sample", self.config.do_sample)
  ...
  if not do_sample:
      # do_sample==False -> greedy decoding
      kwargs = {"do_sample": False, "num_beams": 1}
  ```

**Explanation:** The trainer passes `val_kwargs.do_sample` down via `meta_info`, and the HF rollout maps `do_sample=False` to greedy decoding, but nothing in the agent-loop/vLLM path reads `do_sample`. Greedy validation therefore depends *entirely* on the operator also setting `val_kwargs.temperature: 0` (and `top_k: -1`, `top_p: 1.0`). In this run the generated trainer YAML (`rollout.yaml:151-167` defaults, temperature 0 / do_sample False — confirmed in `_generated_ppo_trainer.yaml:285-291`) did set temperature 0, and vLLM treats `temperature=0` as greedy, so validation was genuinely greedy here. But if someone sets `val_kwargs: {do_sample: false, temperature: 0.7}` (a perfectly readable config), validation silently samples at 0.7. Note also that even the temperature=0 route does not force top_k=-1/top_p=1.0 — with temperature 0 in vLLM this is harmless (argmax), but the contract is broken.

**Verdict:** Real bug (latent config-contract violation). Benign for this specific run. It did **not** cause validation accuracy 0.0 — with temperature 0 the model was decoded greedily and still produced no correct answers, consistent with the collapsed policy emitting 1024-token non-terminating outputs. Validation accuracy 0.0 is a *symptom* of the same degeneration seen in training, not a validation-path bug.

## 2. finish_reason "stop" vs "length" collapsed — REAL BUG (observability; masks truncation)

**File/lines:**
- `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py:664-671`:
  ```python
  finish_reason = final_res.outputs[0].finish_reason
  if finish_reason == "abort":
      stop_reason = "aborted"
  elif finish_reason in ("stop", "length"):
      stop_reason = "completed"
  ```
- `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework/verl/workers/rollout/schemas.py:683-688` — finalize treats STOP and LENGTH identically (`pass` in both branches).

**Explanation:** vLLM distinguishes natural EOS termination (`finish_reason="stop"`) from hitting `max_tokens` (`finish_reason="length"`). verl maps both to `stop_reason="completed"`, and the downstream schema treats them as no-ops. The trainer therefore has no direct signal that a rollout was truncated; the only proxy is `clip_ratio = mean(response_length == max_response_length)` (`metric_utils.py:556-561`). In this run that proxy is what revealed the collapse. Nothing in the reward placement, masking, or log-prob path distinguishes truncated responses either — the mask covers all 1024 tokens including the non-EOS last token, which is *correct* for GRPO math (the probability of the truncated sequence is still the product of its token probabilities), but it means the policy receives zero gradient pressure against degenerating into infinite repetitions except through reward (which went to 0 — a local optimum the loss cannot escape once all group members tie at reward 0 and identical truncation).

**Verdict:** Real bug as an observability/masking-of-symptoms defect; does not corrupt GRPO math itself. It directly explains why the only visible symptom of "no EOS ever" was a metric, not a stop-reason field.

## 3. EOS/stop-token wiring in the vLLM single-turn path — BENIGN (verified against installed vLLM 0.17.0)

**Files/lines:**
- `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py:583-585`:
  ```python
  sampling_params["logprobs"] = 0 if sampling_params.pop("logprobs", False) else None
  sampling_params.setdefault("repetition_penalty", ...)
  sampling_params.setdefault("ignore_eos", self.config.get("ignore_eos", False))
  ```
  No `stop_token_ids`/`eos_token_id` is injected on the single-turn path (stop-token injection exists only in `tool_agent_loop.py:229-232` via the tool parser — irrelevant to GSM8K single-turn).
- `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py:1021-1031` — `_get_override_generation_config` returns only `dict(temperature, top_k, top_p, repetition_penalty=1.0, max_new_tokens=response_length)`; no eos.
- Installed vLLM: `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/config/model.py:1329-1337` — `available_params = ["repetition_penalty", "temperature", "top_k", "top_p", "min_p", "max_new_tokens"]` for `get_diff_sampling_param`; **eos_token_id is not overridable**, so verl's `override_generation_config` JSON cannot clobber EOS.
- Installed vLLM: `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/sampling_params.py:511-536` — `update_from_generation_config`: `if not self.ignore_eos: self._eos_token_id = eos_token_id`, and generation-config eos ids (int or list) are merged into `stop_token_ids`.
- Installed vLLM: `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py:292-297` — per request: `sampling_params = params.clone()` then `sampling_params.update_from_generation_config(self.generation_config_fields, self.renderer.get_eos_token_id())`, where `generation_config_fields` comes from the model repo's `generation_config.json` (input_processor.py:55).

**Explanation:** Because verl leaves `ignore_eos=False`, every request's SamplingParams receives the model repo's EOS (both the tokenizer's eos and any `generation_config.json` eos list, e.g. Qwen's `<|endoftext|>` and `<|im_end|>`). Termination is fully delegated to the model's own EOS emission. For Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat this is the correct wiring. The observed never-EOS behavior means the *policy itself* stopped emitting EOS — a training-dynamics problem (out of audit scope here; the two background audits cover the loss and actor update), not an EOS-id bug.

**Verdict:** Benign — no wrong stop tokens, no EOS clobbering.

## 4. Default `max_tokens` computation — BENIGN (correct, equals 1024 here)

**File/lines:** `vllm_async_server.py:570-579`:
```python
max_tokens = min(
    self.config.response_length, self.config.prompt_length + self.config.response_length - len(prompt_ids)
)
...
max_tokens = max(1, min(max_tokens, max_possible_tokens))
```
with `max_possible_tokens = max_model_len - len(prompt_ids)` (line ~554). For this run: prompt ~<512, so min(1024, 512+1024−len) = 1024, clamped to ≤ 1536−len. Correct; the "exactly 1024" response length is the configured cap being hit, as expected once the policy stopped emitting EOS.

## 5. `num_turns = 2` hardcoded — BENIGN (explains the constant num_turns)

**File/line:** `single_turn_agent_loop.py:107`: `num_turns=2,`. The single-turn schema counts the user turn + assistant turn as 2 turns. It is a labeling convention, not a doubled-generation bug. `agent_loop_tq.py` / `agent_loop.py` merely propagate it (`agent_loop.py:1076` `__num_turns__`). Verdict: benign.

## 6. Sampling parameters — correctly propagated, not ignored — BENIGN

- `agent_loop.py:590-596`: `sampling_params = dict(temperature=config.temperature, top_p=..., top_k=..., repetition_penalty=1.0, logprobs=config.calculate_log_probs)` — all trainer-config values forwarded.
- `vllm_async_server.py:583`: `logprobs = 0` (sampled-token logprobs, returned post temperature-scaled sampling) when `calculate_log_probs` is on.
- Temperature consistency across train/rollout: the actor recompute path divides logits by the rollout temperature (`transformer_impl.py:886-890`, `logits.div_(temperature...)` with `temperature[temperature <= 0] = 1e-8` guard), and `_compute_old_log_prob` passes `temperature=rollout.temperature` (`trainer_base.py:1297`) — matching vLLM's temperature-scaled sampling distribution and its returned logprobs. No train/rollout mismatch.
- Bypass mode (`trainer_base.py:1288`, `data["old_log_probs"] = data.pop("rollout_log_probs")`) uses vLLM's own logprobs — consistent by construction.

**Verdict:** benign.

## 7. Masking, reward placement, and log-prob shift — correct — BENIGN

- Response mask: `agent_loop.py:778` — `response_mask = response_mask_output["input_ids"] * response_output["attention_mask"]` (right-padded response, mask 1 on real tokens, 0 on pad). Truncated responses are fully masked-1 including the last non-EOS token — correct: those tokens *were* generated and must carry probability mass.
- Reward placement: `agent_loop.py:~1031-1040` — `rm_scores[arange, response_length - 1]` where `response_length = attention_mask[:, prompt_length:].sum(-1)`; for a full 1024-token truncated response this is the last real token. Correct.
- Log-prob shift: `verl/utils/torch_functional.py:598-608` — `response_logits = logits[:, -response_length - 1 : -1]; response = input_ids[:, -response_length:]`. Standard, correct alignment.
- Position ids: `agent_loop.py:890-925` — derived from attention_mask (left-pad prompt), consistent with the Megatron forward.
- Chat template: `agent_loop.py:371-452` tokenizes once with the same HF tokenizer used by training; `_cap_text_prompt_length` (360-369) left-truncates to `prompt_length` with a warning — no silent mismatch.

**Verdict:** benign.

## 8. `rollout_log_probs` edge cases — MINOR REAL BUG

**Files/lines:**
- `single_turn_agent_loop.py:99`: `response_logprobs[: self.response_length] if response_logprobs else None` — an empty list (zero generated tokens, e.g. aborted request) is falsy → `None`.
- `agent_loop.py:1046-1047`: `if inputs[0].response_logprobs is not None:` — the *whole batch's* `rollout_log_probs` is dropped if the first sample happens to be `None` (e.g. first request aborted), silently forcing a full recompute or, in bypass mode, missing fields.

**Explanation:** One aborted or zero-token sample at position 0 disables the bypass log-probs for every sample in the batch. Given `vllm_async_server.py` maps abort to `stop_reason="aborted"` and preemption counters exist, this is reachable in practice under KV-cache pressure. Impact in this run: none visible (bypass recompute path is the default fallback), but it is a correctness landmine.

**Verdict:** Minor real bug (batch-wide drop keyed on `inputs[0]`).

## 9. Variable shadowing in `single_turn_agent_loop.py:67/95` — BENIGN

`output: TokenOutput` is rebound to `output: AgentLoopOutput` at line 95, but the RHS references the old binding, which Python evaluates before rebinding. Cosmetic only.

---

## Bottom line for the observed run

- **What the rollout path did right:** EOS wiring, max_tokens, sampling params, mask/reward/log-prob alignment, temperature consistency, greedy validation (via default temperature 0).
- **What actually happened:** the policy degenerated to never emitting EOS (response_length pinned at 1024, clip_ratio 1.0, reward 0, greedy validation accuracy 0.0). The rollout path neither caused nor guarded against this: there is no truncation-specific penalty, no stop-reason surfaced to the loss, and finish_reason collapse (Finding 2) plus the hardcoded num_turns (Finding 5) made the degeneration visible only through `clip_ratio`.
- **Actionable defects found:** (a) port the `do_sample` → greedy mapping from `hf_rollout.py:56-66` into the agent-loop path (Finding 1); (b) stop collapsing `"stop"`/`"length"` finish reasons in `vllm_async_server.py:668-669` and surface a `truncated` flag (Finding 2); (c) key `rollout_log_probs` propagation on per-sample None-ness, not `inputs[0]` (Finding 8).

The GRPO loss and Megatron actor update — the likely *drivers* of the degeneration (e.g., group-normalized advantage with all-zero rewards, advantage computed on a fully-truncated response) — are covered by the two background audits and were deliberately excluded here.

steps.reasoning_content:
The core loss aggregation matches upstream verl exactly. I've now verified essentially the whole active path.

The remaining thread: check the two background agents' output when they finish. Let me also quickly double-check compute_response_mask and the `kl_penalty` used in losses (already verified: k1/k3 correct).

Also one detail worth double-checking: in `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage`, `scores[i] = (scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]) / (id2std[index[i]] + epsilon)` — in-place modification of `scores` on a tensor that... `scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)` — sum produces a NEW tensor, so in-place is fine. Also `token_level_rewards = token_level_scores` — no aliasing issue since sum copies.

Actually wait — one more thing worth checking in the GRPO path: `id2std` uses `torch.std` (Bessel, n-1). With n=4, fine.

But there's a subtle known issue in the verl GRPO: the advantage is applied to ALL tokens including EOS-adjacent, standard.

The collapse symptoms: reward → 0, lengths → 1024, advantages all zero (all 4 responses per group get same reward 0 → std=0 → adv=0 → pg_loss exactly 0). This is self-consistent: once the model stops producing "#### <number>" (which gsm8k strict extraction requires), reward is 0 for all responses in all groups → all advantages zero → pg_loss exactly 0 → no policy gradient; only KL loss and MoE z-loss remain → kl_loss ~0.2. The question is what pushed the model there. Entropy fell 0.12 — entropy collapse. GRPO with std normalization... standard verl.

One thing to examine: the response_mask includes EOS? get_response_mask: mask up to and including EOS. Length saturation = no EOS produced.

Things that could push to degenerate long outputs:
1. token-mean loss aggregation (standard verl, known to bias toward long sequences vs seq-mean, but not a "bug").
2. The reward being 0/1 with strict extraction — once format drifts, all-zero rewards → zero gradient, no recovery force. Only KL loss remains, which pulls toward reference — but kl_loss observed growing to 0.7 then settling 0.2 suggests drift happened, then KL pulled back but the policy is stuck in a degenerate mode since pg_loss = 0.

Hmm, but the report should focus on code-attested bugs. Let me also verify the async rollout manager's response handling for EOS/stop and whether `rollout_log_probs` is present. The background agent "Audit rollout agent loop" is handling that. Let me wait/check its status.

Actually, let me also check `calculate_debug_metrics` and `compute_rollout_correction...` quickly — already done.

One more possible bug to check: in ray_trainer.py line 1553-1558, `entropy_agg` calls `agg_loss` WITHOUT passing dp_size/batch_num_tokens/global_batch_size — just loss_scale_factor. So for the metric actor/entropy it uses local mean (batch_num_tokens=None, dp_size=1 default). That's a metric only — benign (slightly wrong metric under DP, not a training bug).

Also line 1557 passes loss_scale_factor=actor_config.loss_scale_factor — with loss_agg_mode token-mean, loss_scale_factor is unused. Fine.

Let me check the remaining background agents and the observed_run logs for hints. Actually let me look at the observed_run directory for logged responses to confirm the degenerate output mode.

33	            offload_fraction=0.5,
34	            param_update_in_fp32=True,
35	            overlap_cpu_optimizer_d2h_h2d=True,
36	        )
37	        optimizer.step()
38	
39	    Note:
40	        This optimizer is particularly useful in scenarios where memory
41	        constraints are present or when leveraging both CPU and GPU resources
42	        can lead to performance improvements.
43	    """
44	
45	    def __init__(
46	        self,
47	        params,
48	        offload_fraction=0.5,
49	        cpu_optimizer_cls=None,
50	        gpu_optimizer_cls=None,
51	        param_update_in_fp32: bool = False,
52	        pin_cpu_grads: bool = True,
53	        pin_cpu_params: bool = True,
54	        overlap_cpu_optimizer_d2h_h2d: bool = True,
55	        **kwargs,
56	    ):
57	        super(HybridDeviceOptimizer, self).__init__(
58	            params,
59	            defaults={
60	                "offload_fraction": offload_fraction,
61	                "cpu_optimizer_cls": cpu_optimizer_cls,
62	                "gpu_optimizer_cls": gpu_optimizer_cls,
63	                "param_update_in_fp32": param_update_in_fp32,
64	                "pin_cpu_grads": pin_cpu_grads,
65	                "pin_cpu_params": pin_cpu_params,
66	                "overlap_cpu_optimizer_d2h_h2d": overlap_cpu_optimizer_d2h_h2d,
67	                **kwargs,
68	            },
69	        )
70	
71	        self.offload_fraction = offload_fraction
72	        self.cpu_optimizer_cls = cpu_optimizer_cls
73	        self.gpu_optimizer_cls = gpu_optimizer_cls
74	        self.pin_cpu_grads = pin_cpu_grads
75	        self.pin_cpu_params = pin_cpu_params
76	        self.overlap_cpu_optimizer_d2h_h2d = overlap_cpu_optimizer_d2h_h2d
77	        self.param_update_in_fp32 = param_update_in_fp32
78	        self.sub_optimizer_kwargs = kwargs
79	
80	        self._init_sub_optimizers()
81	        self._register_load_state_dict_hooks()
82	
83	    def _set_sub_optimizer_grads(self):
84	        if self.param_update_in_fp32:
85	            for param in self.param_to_fp32_param:
86	                if param in self.gpu_params_map_cpu_copy:
87	                    # Skip if the param is offloaded to CPU, it should be handled
88	                    # in the following part.
89	                    continue
90	                fp32_param = self.param_to_fp32_param[param]
91	                grad = getattr(param, "decoupled_grad", param.grad)
92	                if grad is not None:
93	                    fp32_param.grad = grad.to(fp32_param.dtype)
94	                    fp32_param.requires_grad = True
95	                else:
96	                    fp32_param.requires_grad = False
97	
98	        # Sync the grads from GPU to CPU.
99	        for optimizer in self.cpu_optimizers:
100	            for param in _param_generator(optimizer):
101	                gpu_param = self.cpu_copys_map_gpu_param[param]
102	                grad = getattr(gpu_param, "decoupled_grad", gpu_param.grad)
103	                if grad is None:
104	                    param.requires_grad = False
105	                    continue
106	
107	                param.requires_grad = False
108	                if param not in self.cpu_copy_map_grad:
109	                    self.cpu_copy_map_grad[param] = torch.empty(
110	                        param.shape, dtype=param.dtype, pin_memory=self.pin_cpu_grads, device="cpu"
111	                    )
112	                    param.grad = self.cpu_copy_map_grad[param]
113	
114	                self.cpu_copy_map_grad[param].data.copy_(grad, non_blocking=True)
115	            self._cpu_optimizer_map_data_event[optimizer] = self._d2h_stream.record_event()
116	
117	    def _register_param_copy_back_gpu_hook(self):
118	        def param_copy_back_gpu_hook_closure():
119	            def param_copy_back_gpu_hook(optimizer, args, kwargs):
120	                self._h2d_stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
121	                with torch.cuda.stream(self._h2d_stream):
122	                    for param in _param_generator(optimizer):
123	                        gpu_param = self.cpu_copys_map_gpu_param[param]
124	                        gpu_param.data.copy_(param.data, non_blocking=True)
125	                self._h2d_stream.record_event().wait(torch.cuda.current_stream())
126	
127	            return param_copy_back_gpu_hook
128	
129	        def fp32_param_copy_back_gpu_hook_closure():
130	            def fp32_param_copy_back_gpu_hook(optimizer, args, kwargs):
131	                for group in self.param_groups:
132	                    for param in group["params"]:
133	                        if param in self.gpu_params_map_cpu_copy:
134	                            # Skip if the param is offloaded to GPU, it has been
135	                            # copied back in the previous hook.
136	                            continue
137	
138	                        if param in self.param_to_fp32_param:
139	                            fp32_param = self.param_to_fp32_param[param]
140	                            param.data.copy_(fp32_param.data)
141	
142	            return fp32_param_copy_back_gpu_hook
143	
144	        for optimizer in self.sub_optimizers:
145	            if optimizer is not self.gpu_optimizer:
146	                optimizer.register_step_post_hook(param_copy_back_gpu_hook_closure())
147	            elif self.param_update_in_fp32:
148	                optimizer.register_step_post_hook(fp32_param_copy_back_gpu_hook_closure())
149	
150	    def step(self, closure=None):
151	        """
152	        Override the step method to perform the following operations:
153	            1. Sync the HDO param_groups to sub-optimizers.
154	            2. Sync the grads from GPU to CPU.
155	            3. Step the sub-optimizers.
156	            4. Sync the sub-optimizers state to HDO.
157	        """
158	        # Sync param_groups to sub-optimizers before each step to make sure
159	        # the lr, wd, etc. are up-to-date.
160	        self._sync_hdo_param_groups_to_sub_optimizers()
161	
162	        self._d2h_stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
163	        with torch.cuda.stream(self._d2h_stream):
164	            self._set_sub_optimizer_grads()
165	
166	        # Step the sub-optimizers.
167	        if self.gpu_optimizer:
168	            self.gpu_optimizer.step(closure)
169	
170	        for cpu_optimizer in self.cpu_optimizers:
171	            d2h_event = self._cpu_optimizer_map_data_event.pop(cpu_optimizer, None)
172	            if d2h_event is not None:
173	                d2h_event.synchronize()
174	            cpu_optimizer.step(closure)
175	
176	        # Sync state and param_groups to HDO after each step.
177	        # NOTE: It is possible for the optimizer to change the properties
178	        #   in param_groups.
179	        self._sync_sub_optimizers_state_to_hdo()
180	
181	    def _init_sub_optimizers(self):
182	        (
183	            self.cpu_param_groups,
184	            self.gpu_param_groups,
185	            self.gpu_params_map_cpu_copy,
186	            self.cpu_copys_map_gpu_param,
187	            self.param_to_fp32_param,
188	        ) = self._get_sub_optimizer_param_groups(self.offload_fraction)
189	        self.param_to_inner_param = {}
190	        self.inner_param_to_orig_param = {}
191	        for group in self.param_groups:
192	            for param in group["params"]:
193	                if param in self.param_to_fp32_param:
194	                    inner_param = self.param_to_fp32_param[param]
195	                elif param in self.gpu_params_map_cpu_copy:
196	                    inner_param = self.gpu_params_map_cpu_copy[param]
197	                else:
198	                    inner_param = param
199	                self.param_to_inner_param[param] = inner_param
200	                self.inner_param_to_orig_param[inner_param] = param
201	        self.fp32_param_to_orig_param = {v: k for k, v in self.param_to_fp32_param.items()}
202	
203	        self.cpu_optimizers = []
204	        if self.overlap_cpu_optimizer_d2h_h2d:
205	            self.cpu_optimizers = self.build_cpu_optimizer_list(
206	                self.cpu_optimizer_cls, self.cpu_param_groups
207	            )
208	        elif len(self.cpu_param_groups) > 0:
209	            self.cpu_optimizers = [self.cpu_optimizer_cls(self.cpu_param_groups)]
210	
211	        if len(self.gpu_param_groups) > 0:
212	            self.gpu_optimizer = self.gpu_optimizer_cls(self.gpu_param_groups)
213	        else:
214	            self.gpu_optimizer = None
215	
216	        self.cpu_copy_map_grad: Dict[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] = defaultdict(torch.Tensor)
217	        self._d2h_stream = torch.cuda.current_stream()
218	        self._h2d_stream = torch.cuda.current_stream()
219	        if self.overlap_cpu_optimizer_d2h_h2d:
220	            self._d2h_stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
221	            self._h2d_stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
222	        self._cpu_optimizer_map_data_event = dict()
223	
224	        self._register_param_copy_back_gpu_hook()
225	
226	    @staticmethod
227	    def build_cpu_optimizer_list(cpu_optimizer_cls, cpu_param_groups):
228	        """Build several cpu optimizers to enable overlap. Currently we naively
229	        assign each parameter to an individual optimizer.
230	
231	        Args:
232	            cpu_optimizer_cls (Type[torch.optim.Optimizer]): A torch optimizer class
233	            cpu_param_groups (List[Dict[str, Any]]): The CPU parameter groups
234	        """
235	        cpu_optimizers = []
236	
237	        if len(cpu_param_groups) == 0:
238	            return cpu_optimizers
239	
240	        for group in cpu_param_groups:
241	            group_defaults = group.copy()
242	            params = group_defaults.pop("params")
243	            if isinstance(params, torch.Tensor):
244	                params = [params]
245	            for param in params:
246	                _cpu_param_group = group_defaults.copy()
247	                _cpu_param_group["params"] = [param]
248	                cpu_optimizers.append(cpu_optimizer_cls([_cpu_param_group]))
249	        return cpu_optimizers
250	
251	    def _get_sub_optimizer_param_groups(self, offload_fraction: float):
252	        params = []
253	        for group in self.param_groups:
254	            params.extend(group["params"])
255	        params_total_numel = sum([param.numel() for param in params])
256	        gpu_params_total_numel = sum([param.numel() for param in params if param.is_cuda])
257	        cpu_params_total_numel = params_total_numel - gpu_params_total_numel
258	        offload_threshold = gpu_params_total_numel * offload_fraction
259	        offload_params_numel = 0
260	        cpu_param_groups = []
261	        gpu_param_groups = []
262	        gpu_params_map_cpu_copy = {}
263	        cpu_copys_map_gpu_param = {}
264	        param_to_fp32_param = {}
265	        for group in self.param_groups:
266	            gpu_group = group.copy()
267	            cpu_group = group.copy()
268	            gpu_group["params"] = []
269	            cpu_group["params"] = []
270	            for param in group["params"]:
271	                orig_param = param
272	                cpu_copy = False
273	                if offload_params_numel < offload_threshold and param.is_cuda:
274	                    param = param.detach().clone().cpu().pin_memory()
275	                    offload_params_numel += param.numel()
276	                    cpu_copy = True
277	                if self.param_update_in_fp32 and param.dtype != torch.float32:
278	                    param = param.detach().clone().float()
279	                    param_to_fp32_param[orig_param] = param
280	
281	                if cpu_copy:
282	                    gpu_params_map_cpu_copy[orig_param] = param
283	                    cpu_copys_map_gpu_param[param] = orig_param
284	
285	                if param.is_cuda:
286	                    gpu_group["params"].append(param)
287	                else:
288	                    cpu_group["params"].append(param)
289	            if len(gpu_group["params"]) != 0:
290	                gpu_param_groups.append(gpu_group)
291	            if len(cpu_group["params"]) != 0:
292	                cpu_param_groups.append(cpu_group)
293	
294	        return (
295	            cpu_param_groups,
296	            gpu_param_groups,
297	            gpu_params_map_cpu_copy,
298	            cpu_copys_map_gpu_param,
299	            param_to_fp32_param,
300	        )
301	
302	    def _sync_sub_optimizers_state_to_hdo(self):
303	        """
304	        Update HDO state attribute to sub-optimizers.
305	        """
306	
307	        # optimizer.state:
308	        # {
309	        #    torch.nn.Parameter: {
310	        #        str: Any,
311	        #    },
312	        #    ...
313	        # }
314	        new_state = defaultdict(dict)
315	        for optimizer in self.sub_optimizers:
316	            for param in optimizer.state:
317	                orig_param = self.inner_param_to_orig_param[param]
318	                new_state[orig_param] = optimizer.state[param]
319	                if self.param_update_in_fp32:
320	                    new_state[orig_param]["master_param"] = param
321	        self.state = new_state
322	
323	    def _sync_hdo_state_to_sub_optimizers(self):
324	        for optimizer in self.sub_optimizers:
325	            new_state = defaultdict(dict)
326	            for group in optimizer.param_groups:
327	                for param in group["params"]:
328	                    orig_param = self.inner_param_to_orig_param[param]
329	                    new_state[param] = self.state[orig_param]
330	            optimizer.state = new_state
331	        self._update_fp32_params_by_new_state()
332	        self._move_new_state_to_right_device()
333	
334	    def _sync_hdo_param_groups_to_sub_optimizers(self):
335	        """Sync HDO new param_groups attribute (e.g. lr, wd, etc.) to sub-optimizers."""
336	        param_in_param_group_index = {}
337	        for i, group in enumerate(self.param_groups):
338	            for p_id, param in enumerate(group["params"]):
339	                inner_param = self.param_to_inner_param[param]
340	                param_in_param_group_index[inner_param] = (i, p_id)
341	
342	        for optimizer in self.sub_optimizers:
343	            new_param_groups = []
344	            for group in optimizer.param_groups:
345	                new_group = group.copy()
346	                # After sync-up the sub-optimizer last update, we need to sync-up the
347	                # HDO new param_groups attributes to the sub-optimizer.
348	                assert len(group["params"]) > 0, "param_groups should not be empty"
349	                group_id, _ = param_in_param_group_index[group["params"][0]]
350	                update_group_attrs = self.param_groups[group_id].copy()
351	                del update_group_attrs["params"]
352	                new_group.update(update_group_attrs)
353	
354	                new_param_groups.append(new_group)
355	            optimizer.param_groups = new_param_groups
356	
357	    def _move_new_state_to_right_device(self):
358	        for optimizer in self.sub_optimizers:
359	            for param, state in optimizer.state.items():
360	                for k, v in state.items():
361	                    if not isinstance(v, torch.Tensor):
362	                        continue
363	                    orig_param = self.inner_param_to_orig_param.get(param, param)
364	                    if isinstance(optimizer, self.defaults["cpu_optimizer_cls"]):
365	                        self.state[orig_param][k] = state[k] = v.to("cpu")
366	                    else:
367	                        self.state[orig_param][k] = state[k] = v.to("cuda")
368	
369	    def _update_fp32_params_by_new_state(self):
370	        if not self.param_update_in_fp32:
371	            return
372	        for param, v in self.state.items():
373	            fp32_param = self.param_to_fp32_param[param]
374	            fp32_param.data.copy_(v["master_param"])
375	
376	    def update_fp32_param_by_new_param(self):
377	        """
378	        Update the fp32 parameters by the new parameters.
379	        """
380	        for param, fp32_param in self.param_to_fp32_param.items():
381	            fp32_param.data.copy_(param)
382	
383	    def _register_load_state_dict_hooks(self):
384	        def pre_load_state_dict_hook(self, state_dict):
385	            """
386	            Pre-load state dictionary hook to prevent loss of precision in
387	            mixed-precision training.
388	
389	            When loading a state dictionary with `torch.load_state_dict`,
390	            optimizer states are reset and cast from `float32` to `bfloat16`/`float16`,
391	            potentially losing precision. This hook replaces parameters with
392	            their `float32` copies to mitigate this issue.
393	
394	            Args:
395	                state_dict (dict): The state dictionary to be loaded.
396	
397	            Returns:
398	                dict: The modified state dictionary with `float32` parameters.
399	            """
400	            if not self.param_update_in_fp32:
401	                return state_dict
402	
403	            new_state = {}
404	            for param, v in self.state.items():
405	                param = self.param_to_fp32_param.get(param, param)
406	                new_state[param] = v
407	            self.state = new_state
408	
409	            for group in self.param_groups:
410	                for i, param in enumerate(group["params"]):
411	                    group["params"][i] = self.param_to_fp32_param.get(param, param)
412	
413	            return state_dict
414	
415	        self.register_load_state_dict_pre_hook(pre_load_state_dict_hook)
416	
417	        def post_load_state_dict_hook(self):
418	            # 1. Replace the temporarily replaced fp32 parameters back. Please
419	            # refer to the documentation in `pre_load_state_dict_hook`.
420	            if self.param_update_in_fp32:
421	                new_state = {}
422	                for param, v in self.state.items():
423	                    orig_param = self.fp32_param_to_orig_param.get(param, param)
424	                    new_state[orig_param] = v
425	                self.state = new_state
426	
427	                for group in self.param_groups:
428	                    for i, param in enumerate(group["params"]):
429	                        group["params"][i] = self.fp32_param_to_orig_param.get(param, param)
430	
431	            # 2. After loading state_dict, the parameters may change, and we need to
432	            # reinitialize the sub-optimizers to regenerate the new parameters and
433	            # cpu copy pairs.
434	            self._init_sub_optimizers()
435	            self._sync_hdo_param_groups_to_sub_optimizers()
436	            self._sync_hdo_state_to_sub_optimizers()
437	
438	        self.register_load_state_dict_post_hook(post_load_state_dict_hook)
439	
440	    def zero_grad(self, set_to_none: bool = True):
441	        """
442	        Zero or zero to none the gradients of all the parameters in the model.
443	        """
444	        super(HybridDeviceOptimizer, self).zero_grad(set_to_none)
445	        for group in self.param_groups:
446	            for param in group["params"]:
447	                if hasattr(param, "decoupled_grad"):
448	                    if set_to_none:
449	                        param.decoupled_grad = None
450	                    else:
451	                        param.decoupled_grad.zero_()
452	
453	    def dummy_step(self):
454	        """
455	        The dummy step can be used to initialize the potential optimizer.state,
456	        which can solve the problem of checkpoint loading for an inplace operation
457	        such as loading a torch distributed checkpoint, for example.
458	        """
459	        for group in self.param_groups:
460	            for param in group["params"]:
461	                param.grad = torch.randn_like(param)
462	        self.step()
463	        self.zero_grad()
464	
465	    @property
466	    def sub_optimizers(self):
467	        """
468	        Return the list of sub-optimizers.
469	        """
470	        if self.gpu_optimizer is not None:
471	            return self.cpu_optimizers + [self.gpu_optimizer]
472	        return self.cpu_optimizers

Key data so far:
- corr_kl (KL between vLLM rollout log probs and training old log probs) stays ~0.010-0.015 through step 60 — NOT growing. So the weight sync is correct; the engines agree. That kills the "weights not synced to vLLM" hypothesis. Good.

- ppo_kl stays tiny ~±0.001 (on-policy single epoch — expected).
- pg_clipfrac tiny (0.001-0.019) — ratio near 1 during the update (single PPO epoch, micro-batches... wait clipfrac is computed over all tokens? It's tiny because with one epoch and mini-batch 1? Actually actor.ppo_clipfrac is fraction of tokens where ratio left the clip region during training updates — with global batch 16 and mini-batch... it should be near 0 with on-policy single-epoch. OK).
- entropy rises 0.117 → 0.38 over steps 1-57. This is a big deal: the policy is getting MORE random, monotonically.
- kl_loss (KL to ref, k3 estimator) rises monotonically 0.003 → 0.45 by step 60.
- score stays noisy 0.06-0.69 with no upward trend.
- grad_norm 55-250 vs clip 1.0.

The rising entropy + rising KL-to-ref with no reward improvement is the signature of a policy-gradient that is dominated by noise/bias pushing toward entropy maximization. In GRPO with std-normalized advantages, the whitened advantage has mean 0 per group and std 1 per group; for a 0/1 reward with group [0,0,0,0] or [1,1,1,1], advantage = 0 (fallback mean=0,std=1 → (r-mean)/std = 0). For mixed groups, advantages are ±(something)/std.

Now — a key mechanism to check: whitening makes advantage magnitude ~1 even when reward differences are pure noise. With 4 groups of 4 and 0/1 rewards, GRPO amplifies pure noise to advantage ±1.5. The policy gradient then pushes up random tokens of lucky samples and down random tokens of unlucky ones — this is a zero-mean random perturbation of logits, which INCREASES entropy (random walk in logit space = entropy increase + KL drift). This is a known GRPO-without-baseline weakness, not a code bug.

BUT the observed collapse to length 1024 needs a systematic driver. In vanilla PPO with token-mean loss: all tokens of a positive-advantage sample get positive gradient, weighted equally. Longer sequences have MORE tokens but each token has weight 1/batch_num_tokens — so total gradient magnitude per sequence ∝ its length (more tokens × same per-token weight). With advantage normalized per group (not per length), a long degenerate sample with positive advantage gets a bigger total push... but that's uniform across its tokens.

Hmm — is there anything in the ACTIVE path that would favor long responses? Let me reconsider the sign/scale checks on the response_mask vs EOS. One candidate: `get_response_mask` includes the first EOS token in the mask (mask up to and INCLUDING first EOS: `(eos_mask.cumsum(dim=1) - eos_mask).eq(0)` — wait let me re-derive: this yields True where cumsum-before < 1, i.e., positions before the first EOS EXCLUSIVE of EOS? eos_mask.cumsum(dim=1) is inclusive cumsum; minus eos_mask gives exclusive cumsum. .eq(0) → True where no EOS has occurred before this position → excludes the EOS position itself. Hmm — at the EOS position, exclusive-cumsum is 0 (EOS not yet counted) → .eq(0) True → INCLUDES the first EOS. Let me check: position i where eos_mask[i]=1, eos_mask[:i]=0 → cumsum[i]=1, eos_mask[i]=1 → exclusive cumsum = 0 → True. So mask includes the first EOS. OK standard.

Another candidate driver of length explosion: reward placement at valid_response_length-1 (last token). For truncated responses (no EOS), valid_response_length = 1024 (all tokens valid). Reward placed at token 1023. Fine.

What about the score being computed on decoded response WITHOUT special tokens — truncated responses just have no "####" → score 0. So as entropy rises, quality degrades → all-zero rewards → zero advantages → no pg signal → only KL pull remains. The length saturation is then... hmm, but why would lengths GROW to 1024 if advantages are zero from step ~97? The length growth started around step 82-106, BEFORE/DURING the final collapse. With entropy rising, P(no EOS within 1024) grows — longer responses. Rising entropy naturally produces length growth (EOS probability per token drops). So entropy rise explains length growth AND reward collapse coherently. 

So the central question for a bug-hunt: is there code that actively pushes entropy UP? With entropy_coeff = 0.0 and no entropy term, the only gradient is pg_loss + 0.001×KL(k3 toward ref). GRPO whitened advantages on 0/1 rewards = noise amplification → random-walk entropy growth. Combined with Adam being scale-invariant (clip_grad 1.0 vs grad_norm 200 doesn't matter — this is worth noting as a real observation: the clip is ineffective, but Adam normalizes anyway).

So effective lr on the normalized gradient is 1e-6. Over 150 steps that's a total movement of at most 150 * 1e-6 in parameter-space norm — tiny. Yet entropy quadrupled? That suggests the policy change is NOT coming from the optimizer path but from somewhere else... OR that grad_norm is computed differently (e.g., MoE z-loss / aux loss large magnitude but pg part small).

Wait — actually, entropy rising from 0.117 to 0.40 while kl_loss (KL to ref) grows to 0.7: the training-policy log-probs drift from ref. And rollout_corr/kl (vLLM vs training policy) stays ~0.01, so the drift is real in the weights, not a rollout/training mismatch. But with clipped grad norm 1.0 and lr 1e-6, can the weights drift that far in 150 steps? Movement per step ≤ lr × clipped norm = 1e-6 × 1 = 1e-6 in L2. 150 steps → 1.5e-4 total. That cannot produce KL 0.7 per token... unless the model is extremely sensitive, or... the clip_grad isn't actually applied! grad_norm 55-250 is the norm BEFORE clipping; if clipping is applied the metric typically still shows pre-clip norm. So we can't tell from metrics whether clipping is applied. Hmm.

But actually, hold on — this is a MoE model with bf16. And there's the mcore MoE z-loss. Also — the entropy increase is the signature of the model drifting to a flatter distribution.

Actually, let me reconsider: KL(ref||policy) per token of 0.7 is huge. With 150 steps of updates whose per-step ppo_kl is ~1e-4 (per token log-prob movement per update), the sum over 150 steps would be ~0.015 in log-prob movement. KL ~ (Δlogp)²/2 scale for small drift — (0.015)² is 1e-4, not 0.7. So the drift is NOT explained by the pg/kl gradient updates. Something else is moving the weights dramatically.

What could move weights outside the tiny clipped-gradient path?

Candidates:
1. The mcore schedule legacy 2-tuple branch: `output_tensor *= cp_group_size` — a 2x loss scale under CP=2, but that's only a constant factor.
2. `MoEAuxLossAutoScaler` with z-loss — mcore aux losses get injected into the backward via the main backward on the router logits with a loss scale. With calculate_per_token_loss and set_loss_scale(1.0)... but the actual aux loss magnitude is added into activation gradients. The moe_z_loss_coeff=0.001 with 60 experts. That's a load-balancing regularizer, shouldn't cause drift per se.
3. Optimizer state / weight decay? Probably none configured.
4. THE ROLLOUT-WEIGHT SYNC: rollout_corr/kl small means vLLM weights == Megatron weights at each step (they're synced from the actor). That doesn't tell us about drift from ref; both drift together. Consistent.

So the weights ARE moving a lot (kl_loss 0.7), while ppo_kl per update is 1e-4. Contradiction? Not necessarily: ppo_kl is the per-token (log_prob - old_log_prob) on RESPONSE tokens for the current minibatch, measured in the same step's update. The actor is updated with ppo epochs=1, so per-step movement in log-prob on its own training tokens is small by construction (clipped ratio ~1). But KL to the REFERENCE accumulates: each step moves log-probs by ~1e-3-ish on the response tokens... but sum over steps only on the distribution actually sampled. Hmm, but KL(ref||π) measured on current response tokens of 0.7 per token means the average per-token log-prob differs from ref by a lot. If per-step movement is 1e-4 and steps are 150, you can't get 0.7 by accumulation unless movement per step on the relevant tokens is ~0.005+. Actually ppo_kl is the mean per token of (logp_new - logp_old) AFTER the update (log_prob computed in the update forward). Wait, in verl, ppo_kl = (log_prob - old_log_prob) mean over mask — that's exactly the per-step per-token movement. Mean 1e-4... but the MEAN can be near zero while positive and negative cancel. kl_loss is 0.003 initially and grows to 0.73 by step 74 — growth of ~0.01 per step. Per-step KL growth 0.01 with per-step mean Δlogp 1e-4... For KL ≈ Var-ish, (Δlogp)² scale: 0.01 KL per step requires Δlogp std ~ 0.14 per step. But ppo_kl mean is 1e-4 — a mean can hide a large std. There's no ppo_kl std metric. pg_clipfrac ~0.002 means almost NO tokens have ratio outside [1±eps]... wait clipfrac counts tokens where the clipped and unclipped objectives differ, i.e., |ratio-1| > 1.8-ish (clip_ratio 0.2 with dual clip). Ratio = exp(Δlogp). clipfrac 0.002 means ~0.2% of tokens have |Δlogp| > ~0.2. So Δlogp is small for 99.8% of tokens. Then KL growth 0.01/step cannot come from the policy gradient update...

UNLESS: kl_loss is measured BEFORE the update (ref vs current weights at the time of the forward), and the drift comes from something else entirely. What else changes the weights every step? The MoE z-loss? No — that's part of the training loss gradient, still clipped.

Hmm wait — is clip_grad actually applied? If the clip is NOT applied (e.g., a bug where clip_grad config isn't passed to the Megatron optimizer, or grad_norm metric is post-clip), then raw gradient norms of 55-250 with lr 1e-6 → parameter movement 5.5e-5–2.5e-4 per step in L2 norm; over 150 steps with consistent direction, 0.01–0.04 L2 movement — enough to produce per-token KL of ~0.7? For a 7B-param model, an L2 movement of 0.01 spread over all params is tiny... log-prob sensitivity though: gradient norm 223 means d(loss)/d(w) L2 = 223; a step of w move 223*1e-6=2.2e-4 in the gradient direction changes loss by ~223*2.2e-4 = 0.05 (first-order). Loss here includes KL term 0.001*kl... the pg term. Per-token logp change ~1e-3-1e-2. Accumulating coherently over 150 steps: 0.15-1.5 → matches kl_loss 0.7!

So the coherent story: gradient updates with unclipped (or ineffectively clipped) norms of 55-250 push the policy steadily; entropy rises (flattening); responses lengthen; eventually rewards collapse to 0; advantages zero; pg_loss zero; only KL gradient remains, which pulls back toward ref (kl_loss declines from 0.73 to ~0.2 — the KL term is the only thing still training, and it reduces drift). No bug was found in the rollout path that would *cause* the collapse (wrong EOS ids, tokenizer mismatch, mask mislabeling, off-by-one in log-prob shift, or silently ignored sampling parameters). The EOS/stop machinery is wired correctly end-to-end: vLLM applies the model's generation-config EOS to every request unless `ignore_eos`, which verl defaults to False. The observed symptom — every rollout hitting exactly 1024 tokens with `clip_ratio=1.0`, reward → 0, validation accuracy 0.0 — is policy degeneration under GRPO, not a rollout artifact. However, the rollout path contains several real-but-latent defects and one serious observability defect that *masked* the collapse:

1. **`do_sample=False` for validation is silently ignored** in the agent-loop/vLLM path (real bug, latent — this run was saved only by the YAML default `val_kwargs.temperature: 0`).
2. **finish_reason "stop" and "length" are collapsed** to the same stop_reason, so the trainer cannot distinguish "model emitted EOS" from "truncated" (real observability bug — this is why clip_ratio 1.0 was the only visible symptom).
3. **Edge-case bugs** in `rollout_log_probs` propagation (aborted/zero-token samples can drop the whole batch's bypass log-probs).
4. `num_turns=2` is hardcoded for single-turn (benign, explains the constant num_turns).

Details follow.

## 1. Validation greedy decoding: `do_sample=False` is never consumed — REAL BUG (latent; benign for this run)

- `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py:631` — writes `"do_sample": self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample` into `meta_info`.


**Explanation:** The trainer passes `val_kwargs.do_sample` down via `meta_info`, and the HF rollout maps `do_sample=False` to greedy decoding, but nothing in the agent-loop/vLLM path reads `do_sample`. Greedy validation therefore depends *entirely* on the operator also setting `val_kwargs.temperature: 0` (and `top_k: -1`, `top_p: 1.0`). In this run the generated trainer YAML (`rollout.yaml:151-167` defaults, temperature 0 / do_sample False — confirmed in `_generated_ppo_trainer.yaml:285-291`) did set temperature 0, and vLLM treats `temperature=0` as greedy, so validation was genuinely greedy here. Note also that even the temperature=0 route does not force top_k=-1/top_p=1.0 — with temperature 0 in vLLM this is harmless (argmax), but the contract is broken.

**Verdict:** Real bug (latent config-contract violation). Benign for this specific run. It did **not** cause validation accuracy 0.0 — with temperature 0 the model was decoded greedily and still produced no correct answers, consistent with the collapsed policy emitting 1024-token non-terminating outputs. Validation accuracy 0.0 is a *symptom* of the same degeneration seen in training, not a validation-path bug.

## 2. finish_reason "stop" vs "length" collapsed — REAL BUG (observability; masks truncation)

**File/lines:**
- `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py:664-671`:
  ```python
  finish_reason = final_res.outputs[0].finish_reason
  if finish_reason == "abort":
      stop_reason = "aborted"
  elif finish_reason in ("stop", "length"):
      stop_reason = "completed"
  ```
- `/user/linjiayin/harbor-runs/2e339a072ccf/workspace/src/framework/verl/workers/rollout/schemas.py:683-688` — finalize treats STOP and LENGTH identically (`pass` in both branches).

**Explanation:** vLLM distinguishes natural EOS termination (`finish_reason="stop"`) from hitting `max_tokens` (`finish_reason="length"`). verl maps both to `stop_reason="completed"`, and the downstream schema treats them as no-ops. The trainer therefore has no direct signal that a rollout was truncated; the only proxy is `clip_ratio = mean(response_length == max_response_length)` (`metric_utils.py:556-561`). In this run that proxy is what revealed the collapse. Nothing in the reward placement, masking, or log-prob path distinguishes truncated responses either — the mask covers all 1024 tokens including the non-EOS last token, which is *correct* for GRPO math (the probability of the truncated sequence is still the product of its token probabilities), but it means the policy receives zero gradient pressure against degenerating into infinite repetitions except through reward (which went to 0 — a local optimum the loss cannot escape once all group members tie at reward 0 and identical truncation).

**Verdict:** Real bug as an observability/masking-of-symptoms defect; does not corrupt GRPO math itself. It directly explains why the only visible symptom of "no EOS ever" was a metric, not a stop-reason field.
